lessons.title: Guess the character from the line
lessons.description: Trade samurai, ninja and elder lines in a guessing game with friends.
lessons.canDo: Follow the meaning of stylised ぜ/ぞ and recognise a performed character.

lessons.title: Play through the gate scene
lessons.description: Read a little fantasy scene, then discuss the cliffhanger.
lessons.canDo: Understand wondering, explanation and older copulas in a short character scene.

grammar.title: Read a bundle of character cues
grammar.formation: Pronoun/form of address + predicate + sentence ending. Recognise わし/拙者 in labelled fictional roles; identify the actual speaker from the scene.
grammar.explanation: Fiction often bundles pronouns, address forms and endings to suggest a role. わし with じゃ can signal a stylised elder; 拙者 with でござる can signal a stylised samurai. These are recognition cues, not proof of a real person’s age, gender or occupation. One actor can perform several roles. Dialect is a real variety, not incorrect Japanese.
grammar.example: 「わしは道を知っておる」と、老人の役が言う。
grammar.translation: The elder role says, “I know the way.”

examples.ja: 「わしは{道|みち}を{知|し}っておる」と、{老人|ろうじん}の{役|やく}が{言|い}う。
examples.en: The elder role says, “I know the way.”

examples.ja: 「{拙者|せっしゃ}は{門|もん}を{守|まも}る」と、{侍|さむらい}の{役|やく}が{言|い}う。
examples.en: The samurai role says, “I guard the gate.”

examples.ja: {配役|はいやく}を{見|み}ると、{両方|りょうほう}をケンタが{演|えん}じている。
examples.en: The casting shows Kenta performs both roles.

grammar.mistake: Do not answer who actually spoke just by the pronoun. Check the actor label and surrounding scene.

grammar.title: Recognise emphatic ぜ and ぞ
grammar.formation: Plain verb/i-adjective + ぜ/ぞ; noun/na-adjective + だぜ/だぞ. Volitional + ぜ can invite a shared action.
grammar.explanation: ぜ and ぞ add an emphatic, often assertive familiar delivery. They can announce an intention, reaction or warning. Fiction may use them to mark a forceful character, but they are not unique to villains or men. This unit practises understanding labelled script lines; teacher and workplace replies continue to use their appropriate register.
grammar.example: この手紙は俺が届けるぜ。
grammar.translation: I’ll deliver this letter, I tell you.

examples.ja: この{手紙|てがみ}は{俺|おれ}が{届|とど}けるぜ。
examples.en: I’ll deliver this letter, I tell you.

examples.ja: {門|もん}の{外|そと}は{危|あぶ}ないぞ。
examples.en: Outside the gate is dangerous, mind you.

examples.ja: この{町|まち}の{英雄|えいゆう}だぞ。
examples.en: That’s this town’s hero, you know.

grammar.mistake: Keep noun/na-adjective だ: 英雄だぞ. Do not infer an occupation from ぜ or change the underlying event meaning.

grammar.title: A marked style still carries a meaning
grammar.formation: Plain verb/i-adjective + わ; noun/na-adjective + だわ in the taught script pattern. Plain phrase + かしら; remove plain noun/na-adjective だ before かしら.
grammar.explanation: In a stylised character line, わ can add a marked delivery, while かしら expresses wondering. かしら often sounds feminine in contemporary media, but this is not a rule identifying an actual person. わ also occurs in different regional and casual styles with different intonation. Decode the whole line and context. This unit doesn’t score rising/falling intonation as a verified audio fact.
grammar.example: 門はまだ開いているかしら。
grammar.translation: I wonder whether the gate is still open.

examples.ja: {門|もん}はまだ{開|あ}いているかしら。
examples.en: I wonder whether the gate is still open.

examples.ja: この{手紙|てがみ}は{大切|たいせつ}だわ。
examples.en: This letter is important.

examples.ja: {今日|きょう}は{休|やす}みかしら。
examples.en: I wonder whether today is a day off.

grammar.mistake: かしら is wondering, not a guarantee or completed action. Do not add だ in the taught noun+かしら form or identify gender from わ alone.

grammar.title: のだ connects a statement to its context
grammar.formation: Plain V/i-adjective + のだ/んだ; affirmative noun/na-adjective + なのだ/なんだ. Polite のです/んです.
grammar.explanation: Retrieve the explanatory pattern to give a reason or interpretation connected to the situation. のだ is also common in prose; it’s not exclusively an anime or villain ending. Spoken んだ is normal Japanese. Affirmative nouns/na-adjectives require な, while negative じゃない attaches directly. Context supplies the explanatory link; のだ doesn’t make a mistaken claim true.
grammar.example: 道を知らない。初めてこの王国に来たのだ。
grammar.translation: I don’t know the way. The thing is, this is my first visit to this kingdom.

examples.ja: {道|みち}を{知|し}らない。{初|はじ}めてこの{王国|おうこく}に{来|き}たのだ。
examples.en: I don’t know the way. The thing is, this is my first visit to this kingdom.

examples.ja: {彼|かれ}は{勇者|ゆうしゃ}なのだ。だから{冒険|ぼうけん}に{出|で}る。
examples.en: He is the hero. That’s why he goes on the adventure.

examples.ja: {魔法|まほう}は{使|つか}えないんだ。
examples.en: The thing is, I cannot use magic.

grammar.mistake: 勇者なのだ requires な. のだ is explanatory, not an automatic cause marker like ので and not proof that a statement is factual.

grammar.title: Recognise two stylised older copulas
grammar.formation: Fictional elder: N/na-adjective + じゃ (=だ); V/i-adjective + のじゃ for explanatory のだ. Samurai: N/na-adjective + でござる (=である/です here).
grammar.explanation: In this script, noun + じゃ replaces the modern copula だ and noun + でござる creates an older samurai-style statement. A verb is not followed by the same でござる template: the taught noun phrase is 門番でござる. These forms are recognition only. じゃ also has real dialect uses; don’t label all users as elderly. Neither is the contraction じゃん or the negative じゃない.
grammar.example: ここは王国の門じゃ。
grammar.translation: This is the kingdom’s gate. (stylised elder)

examples.ja: ここは{王国|おうこく}の{門|もん}じゃ。
examples.en: This is the kingdom’s gate. (stylised elder)

examples.ja: {拙者|せっしゃ}は{門番|もんばん}でござる。
examples.en: I’m the gatekeeper. (stylised samurai)

examples.ja: この{道|みち}を{進|すす}むのじゃ。
examples.en: You are to follow this road. (stylised elder explanatory instruction)

grammar.mistake: Do not read じゃ as じゃない. Keep で in 門番でござる; recognise the quoted style without using it as a modern business-politeness model.

dialogues.title: A character-line guessing game
dialogues.scene: At home, Misaki, Kenta and Bao play a character-line guessing game. Kenta performs the samurai and elder; Misaki plays the princess; Bao plays the ninja. They use no costumes.

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: {前|まえ}は{早口|はやくち}の{語尾|ごび}を{聞|き}き{逃|のが}しちゃったね。{今日|きょう}は{短|みじか}い{台本|だいほん}で{遊|あそ}ぼうよ。
lines.romaji: Mae wa hayakuchi no gobi o kikinogashichatta ne. Kyō wa mijikai daihon de asobō yo.
lines.meaning: We missed those fast endings last time. Let’s play with a short script today.

lines.speaker: Kenta
lines.line: いいね。{僕|ぼく}は{侍|さむらい}と{老人|ろうじん}。ミサキは{姫|ひめ}で、バオは{忍者|にんじゃ}ね。
lines.romaji: Ii ne. Boku wa samurai to rōjin. Misaki wa hime de, Bao wa ninja ne.
lines.meaning: Sounds fun. I’ll do the samurai and the elder. Misaki, you’re the princess; Bao, you’re the ninja.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: {仮装|かそう}はなしで、{台詞|せりふ}だけで{当|あ}てるんだね。じゃ、{先|さき}に{演|えん}じてみてよ。
lines.romaji: Kasō wa nashi de, serifu dake de ateru n da ne. Ja, saki ni enjite mite yo.
lines.meaning: No costumes—just guess from the lines? Go on, give us the first one.

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: {配役|はいやく}はメモしとくね。ケンタの{一人|ひとり}{二役|ふたやく}、{間違|まちが}えちゃいそう。
lines.romaji: Haiyaku wa memo shitoku ne. Kenta no hitori futayaku, machigaechaisō.
lines.meaning: I’ll note down the roles. I’m going to mix up Kenta’s two characters.

lines.speaker: Kenta
lines.line: 「{拙者|せっしゃ}は{門番|もんばん}でござる。ここは{通|とお}せぬ！」さて、{誰|だれ}でしょう？
lines.romaji: Sessha wa monban de gozaru. Koko wa tōsenu! Sate, dare deshō?
lines.meaning: “I’m the gatekeeper. You shall not pass!” So, who am I?

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: {侍|さむらい}！ じゃ、{次|つぎ}は{俺|おれ}ね。「この{手紙|てがみ}は{俺|おれ}が{届|とど}けるぜ。{任|まか}せとけ！」
lines.romaji: Samurai! Ja, tsugi wa ore ne. Kono tegami wa ore ga todokeru ze. Makasetoke!
lines.meaning: The samurai! My turn. “I’ll deliver this letter. Leave it to me!”

lines.speaker: Kenta
lines.line: {忍者|にんじゃ}だね。「ここは{町|まち}の{門|もん}じゃ。{夜|よる}には{閉|し}まるのじゃ」。これは{簡単|かんたん}かな？
lines.romaji: Ninja da ne. Koko wa machi no mon ja. Yoru ni wa shimaru no ja. Kore wa kantan kana?
lines.meaning: The ninja. “This is the town gate. It closes at night.” Is this one too easy?

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: {老人|ろうじん}！ 「じゃ」が{口癖|くちぐせ}みたい。{標準語|ひょうじゅんご}なら「ここは{町|まち}の{門|もん}だ」だね。
lines.romaji: Rōjin! Ja ga kuchiguse mitai. Hyōjungo nara koko wa machi no mon da da ne.
lines.meaning: The elder! “Ja” is like his catchphrase. In standard Japanese, that’s “This is the town gate.”

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: {姫|ひめ}の{台詞|せりふ}も{聞|き}きたいな。{次|つぎ}の{場面|ばめん}、みんなで{朗読|ろうどく}しようよ。
lines.romaji: Hime no serifu mo kikitai na. Tsugi no bamen, minna de rōdoku shiyō yo.
lines.meaning: I want to hear the princess too. Let’s all read the next scene.

lines.speaker: Kenta
lines.line: じゃ、{今度|こんど}は{止|と}めずに{行|い}くぞ。{手紙|てがみ}を{渡|わた}すところまでね。
lines.romaji: Ja, kondo wa tomezu ni iku zo. Tegami o watasu tokoro made ne.
lines.meaning: Okay, let’s go without stopping this time. Up to the part where we hand over the letter.

dialogues.title: A fictional gate; real actors
dialogues.scene: The friends read their assigned roles in a fantasy scene at a closed gate, then stop at the cliffhanger. The elder says to leave tomorrow; the ninja has not delivered the letter yet.

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: 「{門|もん}はまだ{開|あ}いているかしら。{急|いそ}がなくてはいけないわ」。
lines.romaji: Mon wa mada aite iru kashira. Isoganakute wa ikenai wa.
lines.meaning: “I wonder if the gate’s still open. We must hurry.”

lines.speaker: Kenta
lines.line: 「{門|もん}は{閉|し}まっておる。{冒険|ぼうけん}に{出|で}るのは{明日|あした}じゃ。{今夜|こんや}はここで{休|やす}むのじゃ」。
lines.romaji: Mon wa shimatte oru. Bōken ni deru no wa ashita ja. Kon’ya wa koko de yasumu no ja.
lines.meaning: “The gate is closed. We leave on our adventure tomorrow. Rest here tonight.”

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: 「ならば、{手紙|てがみ}を{渡|わた}すまで{待|ま}つぞ。{朝|あさ}になったら、すぐ{出発|しゅっぱつ}するぜ」。
lines.romaji: Naraba, tegami o watasu made matsu zo. Asa ni nattara, sugu shuppatsu suru ze.
lines.meaning: “Then I’ll wait until I hand over the letter. At dawn, I’ll leave straight away.”

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: 「ありがとう。この{手紙|てがみ}は{大切|たいせつ}だわ。{王国|おうこく}の{運命|うんめい}がかかっているの」。
lines.romaji: Arigatō. Kono tegami wa taisetsu da wa. Ōkoku no unmei ga kakatte iru no.
lines.meaning: “Thank you. This letter is precious. The kingdom’s fate depends on it.”

lines.speaker: Kenta
lines.line: 「おぬしは{勇者|ゆうしゃ}なのじゃ。{魔法|まほう}が{使|つか}えなくても、{道|みち}を{知|し}っておる」。
lines.romaji: Onushi wa yūsha na no ja. Mahō ga tsukaenakute mo, michi o shitte oru.
lines.meaning: “You are the hero. Even without magic, you know the road.”

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: 「{魔法|まほう}は{使|つか}えないのだ。だが、{手紙|てがみ}は{必|かなら}ず{届|とど}けるぞ！」…ここまで？
lines.romaji: Mahō wa tsukaenai no da. Daga, tegami wa kanarazu todokeru zo! Koko made?
lines.meaning: “I can’t use magic. But I’ll deliver the letter!” …Is that where we stop?

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: うん。{結末|けつまつ}が{書|か}いてないじゃん。{続|つづ}き、どうなるのかな。
lines.romaji: Un. Ketsumatsu ga kaitenai jan. Tsuzuki, dō naru no kana.
lines.meaning: Yeah. There’s no ending written here! I wonder what happens next.

lines.speaker: Kenta
lines.line: {門番|もんばん}が{悪役|あくやく}だったりして。「{通|とお}すわけにはいかぬ！」とか。
lines.romaji: Monban ga akuyaku dattari shite. Tōsu wake ni wa ikanu! Toka.
lines.meaning: Maybe the gatekeeper’s the villain. “I cannot let you pass!” Something like that.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: {怖|こわ}いなあ。{忍者|にんじゃ}はもう{手紙|てがみ}を{渡|わた}したんだっけ？
lines.romaji: Kowai nā. Ninja wa mō tegami o watashita n da kke?
lines.meaning: That’s scary. Had the ninja handed over the letter yet?

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: まだだよ。{次|つぎ}はその{場面|ばめん}の{前後|ぜんご}も{見|み}てみよう。{姫|ひめ}の{返事|へんじ}も{気|き}になるわ。
lines.romaji: Mada da yo. Tsugi wa sono bamen no zengo mo mite miyō. Hime no henji mo ki ni naru wa.
lines.meaning: Not yet. Next time, let’s watch what comes before and after that scene too. I’m curious about the princess’s reply.

readings.title: Misaki’s note after the guessing game
paragraphs: ケンタとバオへ。{今日|きょう}の{朗読|ろうどく}の{配役|はいやく}を{残|のこ}しておくね。ケンタが{侍|さむらい}と{老人|ろうじん}、バオが{忍者|にんじゃ}、{私|わたし}が{姫|ひめ}を{演|えん}じた。{仮装|かそう}はしていないけど、{台詞|せりふ}だけで{当|あ}てるのも{面白|おもしろ}かった。
{架空|かくう}の{王国|おうこく}の{門|もん}は{閉|し}まっていて、{冒険|ぼうけん}に{出|で}るのは{明日|あした}だと{老人|ろうじん}の{役|やく}が{言|い}った。{忍者|にんじゃ}は{手紙|てがみ}を{渡|わた}すまで{待|ま}つと{言|い}っただけで、まだ{渡|わた}していない。{結末|けつまつ}はこの{台本|だいほん}には{書|か}いていない。
ケンタの{老人|ろうじん}の{口癖|くちぐせ}が{気|き}に{入|い}ったよ。{私|わたし}も「じゃ」を{言|い}ってみたくなっちゃった。{次|つぎ}の{視聴|しちょう}では{場面|ばめん}の{前後|ぜんご}も{聞|き}くね。{手紙|てがみ}を{受|う}け{取|と}った{姫|ひめ}は、どんな{返事|へんじ}をするのかな。ミサキ

glosses.text: 言ってみたくなっちゃった
glosses.kana: いってみたくなっちゃった
glosses.meaning: ended up wanting to try saying it

watch.prompt: Optionally save a character line from your own clip. Note the literal message, role cue, actual speaker and surrounding action. Do not use fictional speech as a model for every real interaction.

recycling.reason: The character guessing game uses useful media words, without squeezing every previous-unit target into performed fantasy lines.

exercises.prompt: Which two roles does Kenta perform?
exercises.explain: Kenta explicitly assigns himself 侍と老人; Misaki and Bao have the other two roles.

exercises.prompt: How do they play the guessing game?
options: Guess only from the costume colour
Guess the character from a line, without costumes
exercises.explain: Bao says 仮装はなしで、台詞だけで当てる: no costumes, just guessing from the spoken lines.

exercises.prompt: Why did Misaki suggest reading a short script?
options: They had already completed the sequel
They missed fast endings in the earlier viewing
exercises.explain: Misaki says they missed fast endings last time and suggests playing with a short script.

exercises.context: Form practice: keep the noun copula before the named emphatic ending ぜ.
exercises.line: この{人物|じんぶつ}は{武士|ぶし}＿＿ぜ。
exercises.explain: Noun+だぜ keeps the noun copula before the emphatic ending.

exercises.context: Form practice: add the named emphatic ぞ directly to the plain verb, without a noun copula.
exercises.line: {侍|さむらい}が{手紙|てがみ}を{渡|わた}す＿＿。
exercises.explain: Plain verb+ぞ, not 渡すだぞ.

exercises.context: Your friend missed the meaning. Offer to rephrase in standard language and listen again.
exercises.line: {意味|いみ}を{聞|き}き{逃|のが}した。
options: {聞|き}き{逃|のが}したなら、もう{全部|ぜんぶ}{分|わ}かったんだね。
{意味|いみ}は{気|き}にせず、{音量|おんりょう}だけ{見|み}よう。
{標準語|ひょうじゅんご}で{言|い}い{直|なお}して、もう{一度|いちど}{聞|き}こう。
exercises.explain: Rephrasing and replay respond to missed meaning; the others falsely assume understanding or dismiss it.

exercises.line: 「{拙者|せっしゃ}は{門番|もんばん}でござる。ここは{通|とお}せぬ！」さて、{誰|だれ}でしょう？
exercises.prompt: Who performs the gatekeeper’s line in this scene?
exercises.explain: Kenta performs this exact line, then invites the others to guess the character.

exercises.prompt: When does the fictional elder say the adventure begins?
exercises.explain: The elder says 冒険に出るのは明日じゃ and tells them to rest here tonight.

exercises.prompt: What does the ninja’s line establish about the letter?
options: He will wait until handing it over; it’s not yet delivered
exercises.explain: The ninja says he will wait until handing over the letter. Misaki later confirms he has not delivered it yet.

exercises.context: Form practice: attach the named wondering かしら to a noun without だ.
exercises.line: {明日|あした}の{朗読|ろうどく}はお{休|やす}み＿＿。
exercises.explain: 休み+かしら in this taught wondering pattern; it doesn’t assert the answer.

exercises.context: Form practice: use the named explanatory のだ after the affirmative noun 勇者.
exercises.line: {彼|かれ}は{勇者|ゆうしゃ}＿＿のだ。
exercises.explain: Affirmative noun+なのだ, not 勇者だのだ.

exercises.context: Recognition/form practice: complete the fictional elder’s positive noun statement with the named older copula じゃ.
exercises.line: ここは{王国|おうこく}の{門|もん}＿＿。
exercises.explain: Noun+じゃ is the stylised copula here. It’s neither affirmative じゃん nor negative じゃない.

exercises.context: You missed a cliffhanger. Ask to replay the surrounding scene to understand what happened.
exercises.line: {手紙|てがみ}、もう{渡|わた}したんだっけ？
options: {場面|ばめん}の{前後|ぜんご}も{聞|き}いて{確|たし}かめよう。
{手紙|てがみ}なんて{出|で}てこなかったよ。
{台本|だいほん}には{人物|じんぶつ}がいないよ。
exercises.explain: Replaying the surrounding scene addresses the missed action; the other replies contradict the script.

exercises.line: 「{門|もん}はまだ{開|あ}いているかしら。{急|いそ}がなくてはいけないわ」。
exercises.prompt: Who wonders whether the gate is open?
exercises.explain: Misaki performs the princess’s exact opening line.

exercises.meaning: The thing is, I cannot use magic. Use the explanatory のだ.
exercises.explain: The negative plain verb 使えない takes のだ directly; noun/na-adjective な is not used here.

exercises.prompt: Who performed the elder role in the casting notes?
exercises.explain: The first paragraph assigns Kenta both the samurai and elder roles.

exercises.prompt: According to the message, what is the delivery status?
options: The ninja has not handed over the letter yet
The elder has torn it up
exercises.explain: The second paragraph explicitly says まだ渡していない.

exercises.prompt: What will Misaki check in the next viewing?
options: What comes before and after the scene
exercises.explain: The last paragraph says 場面の前後も聞く; the ending is not in the script.

words.example: この製品を店で試します。
性能だけでなく、使いやすさも比べます。
品質についての感想を読みます。
保証の期間は一年です。
返品の条件を先に読みます。
電池の交換が必要です。
付属品のケーブルを使います。
この有線の製品には電池がいりません。
無線で音声を聞きます。
家では有線のヘッドホンを使います。
雑音が少ないと、語尾も聞きやすいです。
外の騒音で台詞が聞こえません。
二つの製品の重さを比べます。
軽量のヘッドホンを探しています。
装着してから、耳が痛くならないか確かめます。
操作の方法を説明書で確認します。
音量の調節は小さい音から始めます。
倍速の設定を一倍に戻します。

移動するときの短所も考えます。

軽いことには長時間使う場合の利点があります。
用途は家での朗読の練習です。
実用に合うか、実際に試します。

lessons.title: Read features and trial conditions
lessons.description: Compare two fictional products while keeping specifications separate from an impression.
lessons.canDo: Read additive claims and degree without inventing test results

lessons.title: Choose for a purpose, with a stated condition
lessons.description: Follow negative comparisons, sufficient conditions and the limits of a review.
lessons.canDo: Identify the comparison direction and what remains untested

grammar.title: Add a second feature, without denying the first
grammar.formation: Plain V/i-adjective or noun + ばかりでなく/だけでなく; na-adjective + な + ばかりでなく/だけでなく. The added item often takes も.
grammar.explanation: Both patterns mean not only A but also B. A remains true. ばかりでなく often fits a more formal written review, while だけでなく is common in daily speech and writing; this tendency doesn’t make either universally wrong. Retrieve earlier だけ. This unit doesn’t require the stronger later ばかりか pattern.
grammar.example: この製品は軽いだけでなく、電池もいらない。
grammar.translation: This product is not only light; it also needs no battery.

examples.ja: この{製品|せいひん}は{軽|かる}いだけでなく、{電池|でんち}もいらない。
examples.en: This product is not only light; it also needs no battery.

examples.ja: {音|おと}が{静|しず}かなばかりでなく、{操作|そうさ}も{簡単|かんたん}だ。
examples.en: Not only is the sound quiet; operation is also simple.

examples.ja: {台本|だいほん}だけでなく、{配役|はいやく}も{読|よ}んだ。
examples.en: I read not only the script but also the cast list.

grammar.mistake: Keep な after a na-adjective, but don’t insert な after a noun. Do not choose between grammatical synonyms as if only one could mean addition.

grammar.title: Understand how great the degree is
grammar.formation: Plain V/i-adjective + ほど/くらい; na-adjective + な + ほど/くらい; noun + ほど/くらい. ぐらい is a variant of くらい.
grammar.explanation: A clause can illustrate the degree of the following description: 音が聞こえないほど expresses noise so strong that the sound cannot be heard. Degree ほど and くらい overlap in many positive contexts. Numerical approximation is not an exact measurement or an automatic maximum. This lesson separates a reviewer’s description from the stated measured weight.
grammar.example: 台詞が聞こえないほど、外の騒音が大きい。
grammar.translation: Outside noise is so loud that I cannot hear the line.

examples.ja: {台詞|せりふ}が{聞|き}こえないほど、{外|そと}の{騒音|そうおん}が{大|おお}きい。
examples.en: Outside noise is so loud that I cannot hear the line.

examples.ja: {装着|そうちゃく}していることを{忘|わす}れるくらい{軽|かる}く{感|かん}じた。
examples.en: It felt so light I almost forgot I was wearing it.

examples.ja: {台本|だいほん}を{読|よ}むのに、{十分|じゅっぷん}ほどかかった。
examples.en: Reading the script took about ten minutes.

grammar.mistake: ほど/くらい can both express degree; name the target in form practice. About ten minutes is approximate, not a promise that ten is the upper limit.

grammar.title: Keep the comparison direction in a negative sentence
grammar.formation: A は B ほど + adjective-negative. For example, A は B ほど重くない. Noun B precedes ほど without な.
grammar.explanation: A negative comparison says A doesn’t reach B’s degree on the stated scale. If B weighs 220 g and A 180 g, A is not as heavy as B. It doesn’t say A is heavier, or that every feature of A is better. A comparison with an expectation also reports a shortfall, not a measured universal fact.
grammar.example: AはBほど重くない。
grammar.translation: A is not as heavy as B.

examples.ja: AはBほど{重|おも}くない。
examples.en: A is not as heavy as B.

examples.ja: BはAほど{安|やす}くない。
examples.en: B is not as cheap as A.

examples.ja: {雑音|ざつおん}は{思|おも}ったほど{少|すく}なくなかった。
examples.en: There was not as little noise as I had expected.

grammar.mistake: Track both objects and the adjective. 重くない is not 重い. Do not use the comparison alone to invent a specification.

grammar.title: Recognise an unexpected or minimal example
grammar.formation: Noun + (で)さえ; noun + に/で/と + さえ where that particle remains necessary. Taught action form: V-stem + さえする. Negative predicates can mean not even.
grammar.explanation: さえ highlights an extreme, surprising or minimal example in context. 説明書さえ読まなかった says even the manual was not read; it doesn’t say no reading of any kind ever happened. Preserve a location/recipient particle when its role is needed. An opinion using さえ is not a product specification.
grammar.example: 説明書さえ読まなかった。
grammar.translation: I didn’t even read the manual.

examples.ja: {説明書|せつめいしょ}さえ{読|よ}まなかった。
examples.en: I didn’t even read the manual.

examples.ja: {静|しず}かな{部屋|へや}でさえ{雑音|ざつおん}が{聞|き}こえた。
examples.en: Even in a quiet room, I could hear interference.

examples.ja: {台本|だいほん}の{人物|じんぶつ}の{名前|なまえ}さえ{分|わ}からなかった。
examples.en: I didn’t even know the names of the script’s characters.

grammar.mistake: さえ is not ordinary only だけ. Do not drop a required location で or read a negative example as a completed positive action.

grammar.title: Identify the one condition presented as enough
grammar.formation: Noun + さえ + Vば; noun + さえあれば; V-stem + さえすれば; Vて + さえいれば. Retrieve ば: ある→あれば, 読む→読めば, する→すれば.
grammar.explanation: The speaker presents one condition as sufficient for the stated result. ケーブルさえあれば、この有線の製品で聞ける is conditional on the cable being present and the already described compatible device. It doesn’t assert that the cable has arrived or that every device will work. This is as long as, not even if ても.
grammar.example: 付属品のケーブルさえあれば、この製品で聞ける。
grammar.translation: As long as I have the included cable, I can listen with this product.

examples.ja: {付属品|ふぞくひん}のケーブルさえあれば、この{製品|せいひん}で{聞|き}ける。
examples.en: As long as I have the included cable, I can listen with this product.

examples.ja: {説明書|せつめいしょ}を{確認|かくにん}しさえすれば、{設定|せってい}の{方法|ほうほう}が{分|わ}かる。
examples.en: If I just check the manual, I can find out how to configure it.

examples.ja: {音|おと}が{聞|き}こえてさえいれば、{合図|あいず}を{確|たし}かめられる。
examples.en: As long as I can hear the sound, I can check the cue.

grammar.mistake: Use the stem in 確認しさえすれば, not 確認するさえすれば. A condition doesn’t confirm that its result already happened.

dialogues.title: Try two fictional headphones before buying
dialogues.scene: After the script practice, Misaki and Bao compare two fictional headphones in a shop. A is wired, 180 g, 3,000 yen; B is wireless, 220 g, 5,000 yen. They try each for ten minutes in the same quiet room. The learner’s device has the compatible socket.

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: {台本|だいほん}の{朗読|ろうどく}を{聞|き}くなら、{製品|せいひん}の{性能|せいのう}だけでなく、{装着|そうちゃく}した{感|かん}じも{比|くら}べよう。
lines.romaji: Daihon no rōdoku o kiku nara, seihin no seinō dake de naku, sōchaku shita kanji mo kurabeyō.
lines.meaning: If we want to listen to the script reading, let’s compare not only performance but also how they feel when worn.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: Aは{有線|ゆうせん}で{百八十|ひゃくはちじゅう}グラム、{三千円|さんぜんえん}。Bは{無線|むせん}で{二百二十|にひゃくにじゅう}グラム、{五千円|ごせんえん}だね。
lines.romaji: A wa yūsen de hyakuhachijū guramu, sanzen-en. B wa musen de nihyakunijū guramu, gosen-en da ne.
lines.meaning: A is wired, 180 grams and 3,000 yen. B is wireless, 220 grams and 5,000 yen.

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: Aは{軽量|けいりょう}で、{電池|でんち}の{交換|こうかん}もいらないね。Bの{良|よ}さも、{同|おな}じ{部屋|へや}で{試|ため}してから{考|かんが}えよう。
lines.romaji: A wa keiryō de, denchi no kōkan mo iranai ne. B no yosa mo, onaji heya de tameshite kara kangaeyō.
lines.meaning: A is lightweight and needs no battery replacement. Let’s consider B’s merits after trying it in the same room too.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: {静|しず}かな{部屋|へや}で{十分|じゅっぷん}ずつ{着|つ}けてみたよ。Aは{忘|わす}れるくらい{軽|かる}かった。
lines.romaji: Shizuka na heya de juppun zutsu tsukete mita yo. A wa wasureru kurai karukatta.
lines.meaning: I tried each for ten minutes in a quiet room. A was so light I almost forgot I was wearing it.

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: {前|まえ}の{視聴|しちょう}では、{早口|はやくち}の{語尾|ごび}を{聞|き}き{逃|のが}したね。{今回|こんかい}は{人物|じんぶつ}が{話|はな}す{場面|ばめん}を{同|おな}じ{音量|おんりょう}で{聞|き}こう。
lines.romaji: Mae no shichō de wa, hayakuchi no gobi o kikinogashita ne. Konkai wa jinbutsu ga hanasu bamen o onaji onryō de kikō.
lines.meaning: In the earlier viewing we missed fast endings. This time let’s listen to the character’s scene at the same volume.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: AでもBでも{合図|あいず}は{聞|き}こえた。でも、{外|そと}の{騒音|そうおん}が{大|おお}きい{場所|ばしょ}ではまだ{試|ため}していないよ。
lines.romaji: A demo B demo aizu wa kikoeta. Demo, soto no sōon ga ōkii basho de wa mada tameshite inai yo.

lessons.title: Read bubbles and printed effects
lessons.description: Distinguish a character’s line from sound, movement or feeling described on an original comic page.
lessons.canDo: Identify what is spoken and keep an uncertain interpretation open

lessons.title: Recover a casual line from its context
lessons.description: Read omitted particles, expressive kana and reactions in four original panels.
lessons.canDo: Recover a familiar object particle and read effects without inventing an event

grammar.title: Separate a line from a printed effect
grammar.formation: A speech bubble gives an attributed utterance. Printed 擬音語/擬態語 may describe sound, motion, silence or feeling; read the surrounding panel.
grammar.explanation: This is a reading convention, not a new inflection. A printed effect need not be something a character said. A mimetic word can describe a state with no audible sound. One form can have several meanings, so use the depicted situation and nearby words. Retrieve earlier 台詞, 人物 and 場面.
grammar.example: 吹き出しの台詞を読む。
grammar.translation: Read the line in the speech bubble.

examples.ja: {吹|ふ}き{出|だ}しの{台詞|せりふ}を{読|よ}む。
examples.en: Read the line in the speech bubble.

examples.ja: {雨|あめ}の{背景|はいけい}に「ざあざあ」と{書|か}いてある。
examples.en: The rainy background has the printed effect zāzā.

examples.ja: 「しーん」は{人物|じんぶつ}の{声|こえ}とは{限|かぎ}らない。
examples.en: Shīn is not necessarily a character’s spoken voice.

grammar.mistake: Do not assign every printed effect to a speaker or force every use of one word into a single category.

grammar.title: Read the word with the action it modifies
grammar.formation: Taught combinations: じっと + 見る; にっこり + 笑う; どきどき + する. Some mimetics take と before a verb. Learn the actual combination.
grammar.explanation: Adverbial words describe how an action happens; some also combine with する to name a state. と is common with certain sound or manner expressions, but neither adding と nor adding する works identically for every word. These models teach combinations, not a universal suffix rule. ごろごろ in a sentence about staying home differs from rumbling thunder.
grammar.example: 視線を変えずに、枠をじっと見る。
grammar.translation: Look intently at the frame without changing the direction of your gaze.

examples.ja: {視線|しせん}を{変|か}えずに、{枠|わく}をじっと{見|み}る。
examples.en: Look intently at the frame without changing the direction of your gaze.

examples.ja: ユイがにっこり{笑|わら}った。
examples.en: Yui smiled.

examples.ja: {雨|あめ}の{音|おと}を{聞|き}いて、どきどきした。
examples.en: Hearing the rain, I felt my heart pounding.

grammar.mistake: Do not assume every word ending in り takes する, or every mimetic word represents an audible noise.

grammar.title: Recover the role of an omitted particle
grammar.formation: In familiar casual context, object を or topic は may be omitted: 傘を見た？→傘見た？ Keep the role recoverable; restore particles in explicit form practice.
grammar.explanation: Short casual manga lines may leave out a particle that context supplies. 傘見た？ asks whether someone saw the umbrella; it doesn’t make 傘 the person doing the seeing. Retain particles that distinguish who did what, contrast or a needed relationship. This is recognition, not an instruction to remove all particles or use a casual fragment in a teacher email.
grammar.example: このコマ読んだ？
grammar.translation: Did you read this panel? (casual object particle omitted)

examples.ja: このコマ{読|よ}んだ？
examples.en: Did you read this panel? (casual object particle omitted)

examples.ja: {傘|かさ}{見|み}た？
examples.en: Did you see the umbrella? (casual object particle omitted)

examples.ja: {台本|だいほん}は{読|よ}んだけど、{続|つづ}きはまだ。
examples.en: I read the script, but not the rest yet; the contrasting は is retained.

grammar.mistake: A missing を in clear casual context is not automatically an error. Do not delete と/で/の blindly or invert the actor and object.

grammar.title: Recognise an abrupt ending and a long vowel
grammar.formation: Between consonants, small っ marks a consonant closure. At the end of あっ！ it marks an abrupt cutoff, not a separately spoken つ. ー/〜 may stretch the preceding vowel in expressive writing.
grammar.explanation: Retrieve ordinary small-っ and long-vowel reading. Printed reactions can exaggerate length; they are not models for prolonging every lesson vowel. あっ is a brief reaction, while あー can be drawn out. A longer reaction doesn’t by itself prove anger or happiness; context matters. Read しーん with a long vowel, not as しん.
grammar.example: 「あっ！」と短く声を出した。
grammar.translation: They gave a short Ah!

examples.ja: 「あっ！」と{短|みじか}く{声|こえ}を{出|だ}した。
examples.en: They gave a short Ah!

examples.ja: 「あー、{分|わ}かった」と{言|い}った。
examples.en: They said a drawn-out Ah, I understand.

examples.ja: {部屋|へや}はしーんとしていた。
examples.en: The room was silent.

grammar.mistake: Do not pronounce terminal っ as tsu or treat expressive length as the correct length of a single kana drill.

grammar.title: A reaction or a question is not proof of an event
grammar.formation: Question intonation/？ asks; an exclamation reacts. Read the reply and later panel before treating a guess as a fact.
grammar.explanation: Reuse earlier の？, かな and っけ. A speaker who asks 雷？ has not established that thunder occurred; ごろごろ can also describe another action. A relieved ほっとした needs an event to interpret it. Printed sweat or tears alone doesn’t identify the cause. These are discourse cues rather than a certified JLPT grammar list.
grammar.example: 「雷？」と聞いたが、返事はまだだった。
grammar.translation: They asked Thunder?, but there was no reply yet.

examples.ja: 「{雷|かみなり}？」と{聞|き}いたが、{返事|へんじ}はまだだった。
examples.en: They asked Thunder?, but there was no reply yet.

examples.ja: {傘|かさ}が{見|み}つかって、ほっとした。
examples.en: They felt relieved when the umbrella was found.

examples.ja: どきどきしている{理由|りゆう}は、{次|つぎ}のコマで{分|わ}かった。
examples.en: The next panel revealed why their heart was pounding.

grammar.mistake: A question mark is not a factual confirmation. Do not assign a cause to an emotion from one effect alone.

dialogues.title: A comic page beside the script
dialogues.scene: At the café, Misaki shows Bao an original comic page after the headphone review. They distinguish bubbles and printed effects. They have only read the first two panels; neither knows who is outside the door.

lines.meaning: Want to read this comic next? The drawings are beautiful.

lines.speaker: You

lines.speaker: Misaki

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: そうか。{音|おと}がなくても、どんな{気持|きも}ちか{分|わ}かるんだね。

lines.speaker: You

lines.meaning: There’s sweat and tears in the drawing. Was she scared, or happy? Let’s read on.

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: うん。{吹|ふ}き{出|だ}しの{台詞|せりふ}も{気|き}になるね。

dialogues.title: A missing particle, and the panel after it
dialogues.scene: Bao and Misaki read the remaining original panels. In the comic, Yui asks Ren about her umbrella. Kenta arrives later, wet from the rain; he is unharmed and had stopped to buy bread. They discuss meanings in context, without inventing a thunderstorm.

lines.romaji: Kono hon, parapara mekuru dake de mo wakuwaku suru ne. Saisho no koma, jitto mite miyō.
lines.meaning: Even leafing through this book is exciting. Let’s look closely at the first panel.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: ユイの{台詞|せりふ}は「{傘|かさ}{見|み}た？」だね。きょろきょろ{探|さが}している。この{場面|ばめん}なら、{傘|かさ}を{見|み}たか{聞|き}いているんだ。

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: {外|そと}では{雨|あめ}がぽつぽつ{降|ふ}り{始|はじ}めて、その{後|あと}ざあざあ{降|ふ}っている。ごろごろという{文字|もじ}は、この{場面|ばめん}にはないね。

lines.line: ごろごろって、{雷|かみなり}にも{使|つか}うよね。でも「{家|いえ}でごろごろする」は、のんびりしてるってことか。

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: ドアががたがたと{鳴|な}って、{足音|あしおと}がぴたりと{止|と}まった。{人物|じんぶつ}が{誰|だれ}か、はらはらしながら{読|よ}んだよ。

lines.speaker: Misaki

grammar: terminal small っ and vowel length
watch.prompt: Optionally examine a panel or subtitle from your own media. Recover an omitted role from context; distinguish a guess, spoken line and printed effect.

recycling.reason: Friends respond to a comic and a cliffhanger; unrelated product specifications and interpretation disclaimers were removed.

exercises.prompt: What must be separated from a character’s spoken line?
options: Printed effects that can depict sound or a state
Every word in a speech bubble
The measured weight of the headphones
exercises.explain: They distinguish the bubble’s 台詞 from printed effects; not all printed text was said aloud.

exercises.prompt: What do Bao and Misaki still not know after two panels?
options: Whether the frame contains any lettering
Whether the page is a product specification
exercises.explain: The last line explicitly leaves the person outside unidentified.

exercises.prompt: Why should they read on before interpreting drawn sweat or tears?
options: Every written effect is an actor’s voice
Several causes are possible; the nearby scene matters
exercises.explain: They reject a single automatic cause and check the context.

exercises.context: Notation practice: choose the written short reaction Ah!, ending abruptly without an extra spoken tsu.
exercises.line: {人物|じんぶつ}の{短|みじか}い{台詞|せりふ}は「＿＿！」だった。
exercises.explain: The terminal small っ marks a cutoff; it’s not the full-size つ sound.

exercises.context: Notation practice: choose a drawn-out Aa with the long-vowel bar ー.
exercises.line: {人物|じんぶつ}は「＿＿、{分|わ}かった」と{言|い}った。
exercises.explain: The bar stretches the preceding vowel; the requested printed form is long, not an abrupt cutoff.

exercises.context: Reply casually to Misaki; keep the distinction between printed effect and utterance.
exercises.line: {効果音|こうかおん}の{文字|もじ}も、{全部|ぜんぶ}{人物|じんぶつ}が{言|い}ったの？
options: うん。{全部|ぜんぶ}の{文字|もじ}を{同|おな}じ{人|ひと}が{言|い}ったよ。
{文字|もじ}はないから、{台詞|せりふ}も{読|よ}めないよ。
そうとは{限|かぎ}らないね。{台詞|せりふ}と、{場面|ばめん}の{合図|あいず}を{分|わ}けて{読|よ}もう。
exercises.explain: The first keeps printed effects distinct; the others invent a universal utterance or deny the printed page.

exercises.meaning: Before interpreting the depiction of tears, read the next panel.
tiles: {涙|なみだ}の{描写|びょうしゃ}を
{解釈|かいしゃく}する{前|まえ}に、
exercises.explain: The temporal order is read context before deciding the cause.

exercises.prompt: What does Yui’s 傘見た？ ask in this scene?
exercises.explain: The object を is omitted in casual context; the next panel answers where her umbrella is.

exercises.prompt: Why does Yui smile and feel relieved?
options: Thunder was confirmed by the headphones
exercises.explain: Ren points to the shelf and Yui recognises her umbrella.

exercises.prompt: What explanation does the final panel give for Kenta’s lateness?
options: He was injured in an accident
He was testing the noise-reduction function
exercises.explain: Misaki gives the reason and says it was not an accident.

exercises.context: Explicit form practice: restore the omitted object を in the casual line 傘見た？.
exercises.line: {傘|かさ}＿＿{見|み}た？
exercises.explain: The umbrella is the thing seen, not the place or recipient. The casual version without を was understandable.

exercises.context: Combination practice: report a pounding heart with the taught どきどきする, in the past.
exercises.line: {台詞|せりふ}を{読|よ}んで、どきどき＿＿。
exercises.explain: どきどきした reports the state; no noun-particle を is inserted into this combination.

exercises.context: Reply casually. Interpret ごろごろ from the sentence 家でごろごろする, without inventing weather.
exercises.line: ごろごろって、{必|かなら}ず{雷|かみなり}の{音|おと}なの？
options: うん。どの{場面|ばめん}でも{雷|かみなり}だけだよ。
ごろごろは、{全|すべ}ての{製品|せいひん}の{仕様|しよう}だよ。
この{場面|ばめん}では、{家|いえ}で{何|なに}もしないで{過|す}ごす{意味|いみ}だね。{解釈|かいしゃく}には{前後|ぜんご}が{必要|ひつよう}だよ。
exercises.explain: The home-resting sentence supports lounging, not thunder. The same form has several uses.

exercises.meaning: I read the line as a cue, found the umbrella, and felt relieved.
tiles: {台詞|せりふ}を{合図|あいず}にして、
exercises.explain: The found object supplies a reason for relief; the reaction is not free-standing proof of another event.

exercises.prompt: Whose umbrella is identified in panel 2?
exercises.explain: Yui says 私のだ after the blue umbrella is identified.

exercises.prompt: What is しーん in panel 3?
options: A printed depiction of a silent pause
exercises.explain: It’s marked as an effect and nobody speaks in that panel.

exercises.prompt: Why is Kenta late, according to his line?
exercises.explain: He says パンを買ってた; being wet is separate and he denies injury.

exercises.prompt: What does ごろごろ refer to in Kenta’s last line?
exercises.explain: 家で gives the home-resting context; nothing confirms thunder.

lessons.title: Read a news brief with its source and date
lessons.description: Retrieve reported speech and causes in an original local-news brief.
lessons.canDo: Distinguish a past decision, a reported future event and a historical count

lessons.title: Use the timetable without mixing its quantities
lessons.description: Retrieve decisions, comparison and conditions to choose a fitting activity.
lessons.canDo: Find an activity, cost and deadline while keeping capacity separate from attendance

grammar.title: Keep the source attached to the report
grammar.formation: Retrieve source によると + plain proposition + そうだ/そうです. Noun/na-adjective retains だ before reported そうだ.
grammar.explanation: Identify who supplied a reported statement and when. A report of a future event doesn’t mean the event has already taken place. Reported 開催するそうだ retains する; appearance 開催しそうだ uses the stem and has a different basis. Earlier source/observation lessons remain relevant. No numerical confidence ranking is assigned.
grammar.example: 記者によると、展示は無料だそうです。
grammar.translation: According to the reporter, the exhibition is free.

examples.ja: {記者|きしゃ}によると、{展示|てんじ}は{無料|むりょう}だそうです。
examples.en: According to the reporter, the exhibition is free.

examples.ja: {記事|きじ}には、{土曜日|どようび}に{開催|かいさい}するそうだと{書|か}いてある。
examples.en: The article says it’s reportedly being held on Saturday.

examples.ja: {見出|みだ}しだけでなく、{本文|ほんぶん}も{読|よ}むそうです。
examples.en: They say they will read the main text as well as the headline.

grammar.mistake: Do not drop noun だ or confuse a reported future arrangement with a completed event.

grammar.title: Read a stated cause without inventing a motive
grammar.formation: Retrieve noun + のため; na-adjective + なため; attributive clause + ため. In a notice, に may be omitted. Purpose ために needs a goal context.
grammar.explanation: A stated cause explains an outcome in the article. 施設の修理のため、会場を変えた reports a reason for changing venue; it’s not an intention to make the repair happen. Tense alone doesn’t decide cause versus purpose. Preserve the source’s scope and don’t infer a different cause, such as noise or weather, from nearby vocabulary.
grammar.example: 施設の修理のため、会場を変えた。
grammar.translation: The venue was changed because of repairs to the facility.

examples.ja: {施設|しせつ}の{修理|しゅうり}のため、{会場|かいじょう}を{変|か}えた。
examples.en: The venue was changed because of repairs to the facility.

examples.ja: {見出|みだ}しが{短|みじか}いため、{本文|ほんぶん}で{条件|じょうけん}を{確認|かくにん}する。
examples.en: Because the headline is short, check the conditions in the main text.

examples.ja: {地域|ちいき}について{知|し}るために、{記事|きじ}を{読|よ}む。
examples.en: Read the article in order to learn about the area.

grammar.mistake: A repair cause is not a purpose, and the future event is not confirmed merely by being reported.

grammar.title: A venue decision is not an attended event
grammar.formation: Retrieve V-dictionary/ない + ことになった for a resulting arrangement; V-dictionary/ない + ことにした for a deliberate choice.
grammar.explanation: The organiser arranged to use an indoor hall on Monday; the learner chooses on Thursday to read the panel descriptions. Neither past decision form establishes attendance at Saturday’s event. する/なる is a framing distinction, not a universal inside/outside decision test. This retrieves unit 6 rather than silently adding ことになっている.
grammar.example: 屋内の施設で開催することになった。
grammar.translation: It was arranged that the event would be held indoors.

examples.ja: {屋内|おくない}の{施設|しせつ}で{開催|かいさい}することになった。
examples.en: It was arranged that the event would be held indoors.

examples.ja: {無料|むりょう}の{展示|てんじ}を{先|さき}に{見|み}ることにした。
examples.en: I decided to see the free exhibition first.

examples.ja: {翌日|よくじつ}には{開催|かいさい}しないことになった。
examples.en: It was arranged that the event would not be held the following day.

grammar.mistake: Changing the plan is not attending it; not doing an action is distinct from not making a decision.

grammar.title: Compare the same quantity and the same period
grammar.formation: Retrieve AはBほど…ない and AよりBのほうが…. State the measured quantity, dates and population before comparing.
grammar.explanation: A tally of last year’s visitors is a count of completed visits. This year’s lecture capacity is a limit, not actual attendance, and an application count is not an attendance count either. Compare like quantities before describing increase/decrease. A smaller capacity doesn’t prove fewer people attended this year.
grammar.example: 去年の午後の人数は、午前ほど多くなかった。
grammar.translation: Last year’s afternoon count was not as large as its morning count.

examples.ja: {去年|きょねん}の{午後|ごご}の{人数|にんずう}は、{午前|ごぜん}ほど{多|おお}くなかった。
examples.en: Last year’s afternoon count was not as large as its morning count.

examples.ja: {一昨年|おととし}より{去年|きょねん}の{来場|らいじょう}{者|しゃ}の{方|ほう}が{多|おお}かった。
examples.en: Last year had more visitors than the year before that.

examples.ja: {定員|ていいん}と{来場|らいじょう}{者|しゃ}の{合計|ごうけい}は{同|おな}じものではない。
examples.en: Capacity and the total visitor count are not the same kind of quantity.

grammar.mistake: A table heading supplies scope. Do not compare future capacity with past attendance as a measured trend.

grammar.title: Apply the stated conditions to the right activity
grammar.formation: Retrieve noun + さえあれば or Vば for a sufficient condition within the stated situation. Distinguish a deadline までに from a duration まで.
grammar.explanation: The free exhibition needs no application. The charged lecture requires prior admission and its ticket; ticket possession is sufficient only in that already admitted context. The application deadline is the previous day at five, not a promise of unlimited same-day admission. A decision to apply is not an accepted application.
grammar.example: 受付で名前を確認した後は、整理券さえあれば入れます。
grammar.translation: After the registration desk has confirmed your name, the admission ticket is enough to enter.

examples.ja: {前日|ぜんじつ}の{五時|ごじ}までに{応募|おうぼ}してください。
examples.en: Please apply by five on the preceding day.

examples.en: If you will not take part in the lecture, you don’t need to apply.

grammar.mistake: Keep the prior-admission context. By five is a deadline, not from five or until five continuously.

exercises.meaning: According to the article’s main text, you can read comic panels and speech bubbles on Saturday.

コマと{吹|ふ}き{出|だ}しを

exercises.prompt: What does Bao choose, without attending yet?
options: The free exhibition to read panels carefully
Sunday’s session at a new venue

exercises.prompt: When must a lecture application be made?

Any time Sunday with no capacity limit

options: This year’s lecture has only twenty places

exercises.context: Form practice: describe your own choice with dictionary 見る + ことにした.

exercises.context: Reply casually to Misaki. You only intend to read the free exhibition’s panels.

うん。{日曜日|にちようび}だけは{応募|おうぼ}がいらないよ。

exercises.explain: The exhibition and lecture have distinct entry rules. The other replies transfer the lecture charge or invent Sunday opening.

exercises.meaning: On the day, after your registered name is checked, the admission ticket is enough to enter.

{整理券|せいりけん}さえあれば
exercises.explain: This sufficient-condition statement retains the registered-name context; it doesn’t grant unlimited unregistered entry.

exercises.prompt: You can visit only Saturday 9–9:30 and want no charge. Which activity fits?
exercises.explain: The table lists the exhibition from 9–12, free; lecture starts 10 and costs 300 yen.

exercises.prompt: What was last year’s total, and its change from the year before?

exercises.prompt: Which reader must apply by the stated Friday deadline?

Someone seeking the Saturday script-reading lecture

exercises.prompt: What changed in Monday’s decision, according to Thursday’s article?

The past visitor tally; all activities became free

grammar.title: A plain written predicate: である
grammar.formation: Noun/na-adjective stem + である; negative ではない; past であった. Verbs and i-adjectives keep their plain conjugations.
grammar.explanation: である is a written copula, common in reports and essays. It is not a polite honorific, and it does not make a claim more reliable. In a である-style essay use plain verb endings too: 開催した, not 開催したである. Keep one surrounding written style; a quoted speaker may still say です.
grammar.example: この施設は地域の交流の場である。
grammar.translation: This facility is a place for interaction in the community.

examples.ja: この{施設|しせつ}は{地域|ちいき}の{交流|こうりゅう}の{場|ば}である。
examples.en: This facility is a place for interaction in the community.

examples.ja: {展示|てんじ}は{無料|むりょう}であった。
examples.en: The exhibition was free.

examples.ja: {講座|こうざ}の{定員|ていいん}は{三十人|さんじゅうにん}ではない。
examples.en: The lecture’s capacity is not thirty people.

grammar.mistake: Do not attach である to a conjugated verb or treat it as business keigo. Plain だ and である overlap in written style, but switching casually throughout a short essay weakens consistency.

grammar.title: Link report clauses with a verb stem
grammar.formation: A verb’s ます-stem can link a written clause: 読みます→読み, 変えます→変え, します→し, 来ます→来（き）. Noun/na-adjective + であり links a copula.
grammar.explanation: The stem can carry a continuing clause in formal writing. The final predicate normally provides the overall tense; context still determines sequence or accompanying actions. Read each clause before joining it. In ordinary conversation the earlier て-form usually sounds more natural. A long chain is harder to follow than two short sentences.
grammar.example: 主催者は会場を変え、前日に連絡した。
grammar.translation: The organisers changed the venue and contacted people the preceding day.

examples.ja: {主催|しゅさい}{者|しゃ}は{会場|かいじょう}を{変|か}え、{前日|ぜんじつ}に{連絡|れんらく}した。
examples.en: The organisers changed the venue and contacted people the preceding day.

examples.ja: {記事|きじ}を{読|よ}み、{要点|ようてん}をまとめた。
examples.en: I read the article and summarised its main points.

examples.ja: {展示|てんじ}は{無料|むりょう}であり、{応募|おうぼ}も{必要|ひつよう}ない。
examples.en: The exhibition is free, and no application is needed either.

grammar.mistake: The final clause still needs a predicate. This is a written-style bridge from familiar stems, not a request to speak to friends in unfinished stem clauses.

grammar.title: Acknowledge a fact, then a remaining contrast
grammar.formation: Verb/i-adjective plain form + ものの; na-adjective + なものの or であるものの; noun + であるものの. Past predicates may also precede ものの.
grammar.explanation: ものの acknowledges the first fact but says a contrasting problem or state remains. It often conveys disappointment: the draft exists, but the title is unsettled. It is somewhat written or considered in tone. In the supported patterns here, the next clause describes the actual result or state rather than issuing a request or inviting a future action.
grammar.example: 下書きはできたものの、題名が決まらない。
grammar.translation: The draft is done, but I can’t settle on a title.

examples.ja: {下書|したが}きはできたものの、{題名|だいめい}が{決|き}まらない。
examples.en: The draft is done, but I can’t settle on a title.

examples.ja: {文|ぶん}は{短|みじか}いものの、{意味|いみ}が{分|わ}かりにくい。
examples.en: The sentence is short, but its meaning is hard to follow.

examples.ja: {説明|せつめい}は{簡潔|かんけつ}なものの、{具体的|ぐたいてき}な{例|れい}が{少|すく}ない。
examples.en: The explanation is concise, but there are few concrete examples.

grammar.mistake: A noun cannot take だものの. Do not mechanically replace every けど in friend-chat with ものの.

grammar.title: An outcome contrary to expectation
grammar.formation: Verb/i-adjective plain form + にもかかわらず; noun + にもかかわらず (also であるにもかかわらず); na-adjective + であるにもかかわらず.
grammar.explanation: にもかかわらず presents an outcome that contradicts what the first fact would lead you to expect. It is formal compared with のに and commonly reports an existing or completed situation. Gratitude or criticism can still be conveyed by the context. にかかわらず without も means regardless of and is a different expression, introduced later.
grammar.example: 雨にもかかわらず、大勢の人が来た。
grammar.translation: Many people came despite the rain.

examples.ja: {雨|あめ}にもかかわらず、{大勢|おおぜい}の{人|ひと}が{来|き}た。
examples.en: Many people came despite the rain.

examples.ja: {何度|なんど}も{校正|こうせい}したにもかかわらず、{数字|すうじ}の{誤|あやま}りが{残|のこ}っていた。
examples.en: Despite proofreading several times, a numerical error remained.

examples.ja: {会場|かいじょう}が{狭|せま}いにもかかわらず、{参加|さんか}{者|しゃ}はゆっくり{読|よ}めた。
examples.en: Despite the venue being small, participants were able to read at leisure.

grammar.mistake: Keep も for despite. Avoid an uncertain future prediction or a request as the second clause in these taught uses.

watch.prompt: Optionally read a short essay or report from your own media. Mark its written predicates and one contrast, then retell the main point in ordinary speech.

exercises.prompt: What inconsistency does Misaki notice?
options: です and である are mixed in the draft
The two friends always speak in である
The article uses no plain forms
exercises.explain: She points out mixed written predicates, not a problem with their spoken conversation.

exercises.prompt: Where will Bao try placing the table?
options: At the top left of every photo
At the bottom right of the page
On the wall beside the window
exercises.explain: Bao’s last line says 表は右下に置いてみる.

exercises.prompt: What does the table let Bao give more space to in the main text?
options: A complete list of lecture applicants
An argument that paid lectures should close
exercises.explain: He says the main text can describe 静かに読めたこと.

exercises.context: Form practice: complete the noun predicate in consistent である-style writing.
exercises.line: この{施設|しせつ}は{地域|ちいき}の{交流|こうりゅう}の{場|ば}＿＿。
exercises.explain: A noun predicate takes である; the requested style is explicit.

exercises.context: Form practice: replace 読んで with the ます-stem written connector before the comma.
exercises.line: {記事|きじ}を＿＿、{要点|ようてん}をまとめた。
exercises.explain: 読み connects a written clause; the final past predicate completes the sentence.

exercises.context: Reply casually to Misaki. You want the rough draft to use plain written style.
exercises.line: {下書|したが}きは、{常体|じょうたい}にそろえるんだよね？
options: ううん。{全部|ぜんぶ}「です」にそろえるよ。
うん。{写真|しゃしん}は{二枚|にまい}とも{消|け}すよ。
うん。「です」が{残|のこ}っているところを{直|なお}すよ。
exercises.explain: The first accepts the requested plain style and states the matching revision; the others contradict it or change the topic.

exercises.meaning: The organisers changed the venue and contacted people the preceding day.
exercises.explain: 変え links the first written clause. The final した supplies past tense.

exercises.prompt: What makes this reading event attractive to the writer?
options: Sharing a quiet time without having to talk
Learning that silent visitors are unwelcome
Buying the most expensive lecture ticket
exercises.explain: The first and last paragraphs develop quiet coexistence, including people who prefer silence.

exercises.prompt: What did the first of the two interviewed visitors say?
options: They always read several books at home
Seeing others read made them want to open a book
The lecture was cancelled because of rain
exercises.explain: The third paragraph identifies the visitor who does not usually read at home.

exercises.prompt: Which activity did the writer’s friend attend?
options: A proofreading class at city hall
exercises.explain: The second paragraph states 有料の講座 and describes reading the script aloud.

exercises.prompt: When is the finished revision due?
exercises.explain: Yamamoto explicitly asks for 推敲 by 木曜日の五時.

exercises.prompt: What is still missing from the main text?
options: The name of an organiser they haven’t met
Comments from two visitors already interviewed
A new opinion from every newsletter reader
exercises.explain: Bao has spoken to two people but has not yet added their comments.

exercises.prompt: When will the newsletter come out?
exercises.explain: Friday is layout day; publication is 来週の月曜日.

exercises.context: Form practice: use ものの after the noun 草稿 with the written copula.
exercises.line: まだ{草稿|そうこう}＿＿ものの、{内容|ないよう}は{伝|つた}わる。
exercises.explain: A noun takes であるものの, not だものの or なものの.

exercises.context: Form practice: add the taught despite expression, including も.
exercises.line: {雨|あめ}＿＿、{大勢|おおぜい}の{人|ひと}が{来|き}た。
exercises.explain: Despite the rain is the unexpected outcome; regardless of and because of do not express this requested relation.

exercises.context: Reply politely to Yamamoto. You accept the Thursday-five deadline and will proofread before sending.
exercises.line: {推敲|すいこう}は{木曜日|もくようび}の{五時|ごじ}までに{終|お}えてね。
options: はい。{月曜日|げつようび}の{掲載|けいさい}{後|ご}に{送|おく}ります。
はい。{推敲|すいこう}も{校正|こうせい}もしないで{送|おく}ります。
はい。{校正|こうせい}もしてから、{木曜日|もくようび}の{五時|ごじ}までにお{送|おく}りします。
exercises.explain: Only the first accepts both the deadline and the intended proofreading step.

exercises.meaning: Despite proofreading several times, a numerical error remained.
tiles: {校正|こうせい}したにもかかわらず、
{数字|すうじ}の{誤|あやま}りが
exercises.explain: The first completed action leads to an unexpectedly remaining problem, not a future request.

exercises.prompt: Why did the writer print this essay?
options: To savour its figurative expression and writing style slowly
To prove that screens never suit anyone
To avoid reading during the commute
exercises.explain: The third paragraph gives the purpose: 比喩や筆致をゆっくり味わいたかった.

exercises.prompt: Why does the friend prefer the screen?
options: Its margins can only be written on with a pencil
Text size can be enlarged and the dictionary is easy to open
It has no notifications or other distractions
exercises.explain: The third paragraph gives those two concrete benefits.

exercises.prompt: Which conclusion best matches the writer’s view?
options: Always choose paper regardless of the purpose
Stop reading on trains and read only at home
Choose a reading method to fit the purpose and situation
exercises.explain: The final paragraph explicitly favours choosing for that day’s purpose over fixing one method.

lessons.title: An inference and a commitment
lessons.description: Correct a mistaken inference and track whether an action is blocked or required.
lessons.canDo: Read the scope and polarity of わけ expressions in a specific situation

grammar.title: A tendency, not a rule for everyone
grammar.formation: Verb plain nonpast/i-adjective + ものだ; na-adjective + なものだ. Negative norms often use verb dictionary form + ものではない.
grammar.explanation: This use of ものだ presents a tendency or norm from the speaker’s viewpoint: unfamiliar places can feel confusing. It is not a measured claim about everyone. A personal past habit uses たものだ, a different use; an emotional exclamation also needs its own context. Here the generalisation is then applied to a concrete first-day experience.
grammar.example: 初めての場所では、戸惑うものだ。
grammar.translation: It’s natural to feel unsure in a place you haven’t been before.

examples.ja: {初|はじ}めての{場所|ばしょ}では、{戸惑|とまど}うものだ。
examples.en: It’s natural to feel unsure in a place you haven’t been before.

examples.ja: {自分|じぶん}の{間違|まちが}いは{気|き}づきにくいものだ。
examples.en: Your own mistakes can be hard to notice.

examples.ja: {人|ひと}の{話|はなし}を{途中|とちゅう}で{決|き}めつけるものではない。
examples.en: You shouldn’t jump to conclusions partway through someone’s explanation.

grammar.mistake: Do not read ものだ as a guarantee that every individual behaves this way. Do not use the recollection meaning of たものだ to answer a question about a general tendency.

grammar.title: Requested advice from someone with experience
grammar.formation: Verb dictionary form or ない-form + ことだ. Polite ending ことです is possible; it still gives a recommendation.
grammar.explanation: ことだ presents what the speaker regards as the appropriate thing to do for the stated goal. It can sound firm or authoritative. Ren gives advice after Kenta asks him for help; it is not a default way to order a teacher or supervisor about. This retrieves the advisory use introduced earlier, distinct from the noun こと and emotional expressions ending in ことだ.
grammar.example: 早く慣れたいなら、分からないことを聞くことだ。
grammar.translation: If you want to settle in quickly, ask about what you don’t understand.

examples.ja: {早|はや}く{慣|な}れたいなら、{分|わ}からないことを{聞|き}くことだ。
examples.en: If you want to settle in quickly, ask about what you don’t understand.

examples.ja: {一人|ひとり}で{抱|かか}え{込|こ}まないことだ。
examples.en: My advice is not to take everything on yourself.

examples.ja: {面接|めんせつ}の{準備|じゅんび}なら、まず{自分|じぶん}の{経験|けいけん}を{整理|せいり}することです。
examples.en: To prepare for the interview, first organise your own experiences.

grammar.mistake: Attach the plain dictionary or negative form, not 聞きますことだ. A polite ending does not remove the authoritative nuance; consider the listener and relationship.

grammar.title: Correct an inference without saying the opposite
grammar.formation: Verb/i-adjective plain form + わけではない; na-adjective + なわけではない. To quote a noun proposition, use Nだというわけではない. Casual ending わけじゃない.
grammar.explanation: The speaker rejects a proposed conclusion: asking for help does not mean abandoning responsibility. This need not assert the complete opposite, and it does not mean “impossible,” as わけがない does. Notice the scope of the statement being denied; 全部…わけではない often denies “all,” not “none.” Noun attachments also include の/である in appropriate attributive contexts; the quoted だという pattern here makes the intended proposition explicit.
grammar.example: 質問したからといって、何も分かっていないわけではない。
grammar.translation: Asking a question doesn’t mean you understand nothing.

examples.ja: {質問|しつもん}したからといって、{何|なに}も{分|わ}かっていないわけではない。
examples.en: Asking a question doesn’t mean you understand nothing.

examples.ja: {映画|えいが}が{嫌|きら}いなわけじゃないよ。
examples.en: It’s not that I dislike going to the movies.

examples.ja: {一人|ひとり}で{作業|さぎょう}する{人|ひと}が、{全員|ぜんいん}{専門|せんもん}{家|か}だというわけではない。
examples.en: Not everyone who works alone is an expert.

grammar.mistake: Do not swap わけではない with わけがない. The first rejects an inference; the second can express impossibility or strong disbelief.

grammar.title: A commitment prevents an action; a negative verb reverses it
grammar.formation: Verb dictionary form + わけにはいかない: cannot do it under the circumstances. Verb ない-form + わけにはいかない: cannot avoid doing it. Polite ending わけにはいきません.
grammar.explanation: This pattern describes an action the speaker cannot reasonably take because of an obligation or circumstances, even if physically possible. Leaving a promised draft unfinished differs from being unable to walk out. With ない, the meaning reverses: 確認しないわけにはいかない means the speaker has to check. Read the first verb before deciding whether the action is blocked or required.
grammar.example: 今日は担当なので、先に帰るわけにはいかない。
grammar.translation: I’m responsible today, so I can’t just go home first.

examples.ja: {今日|きょう}は{担当|たんとう}なので、{先|さき}に{帰|かえ}るわけにはいかない。
examples.en: I’m responsible today, so I can’t just go home first.

examples.ja: {約束|やくそく}したから、{校正|こうせい}をしないわけにはいかない。
examples.en: I promised, so I have to proofread it.

examples.ja: {借|か}りた{本|ほん}なので、{人|ひと}に{貸|か}すわけにはいきません。
examples.en: It’s a borrowed book, so I can’t lend it to someone else.

grammar.mistake: 忘れるわけにはいかない forbids forgetting; 忘れないわけにはいかない would say forgetting is unavoidable. Never ignore the negative before わけ.

dialogues.title: A first shift is not a test of doing everything alone
dialogues.scene: After a first shift, Kenta asks Ren how to deal with questions he could not answer. Ren recalls his own first day. Kenta decides to ask the supervisor about the till at tomorrow’s meeting before the shop opens.

lines.speaker: Kenta
lines.line: {今日|きょう}、レジで{分|わ}からないことがあってさ。{聞|き}きたかったけど、みんな{忙|いそが}しそうで。
lines.romaji: Kyō, reji de wakaranai koto ga atte sa. Kikitakatta kedo, minna isogashisō de.
lines.meaning: Something at the till confused me today. I wanted to ask, but everyone looked busy.

lines.speaker: Ren
lines.line: {初日|しょにち}だもんね。{初|はじ}めての{場所|ばしょ}では、{戸惑|とまど}うものだよ。{僕|ぼく}もそうだった。
lines.romaji: Shonichi da mon ne. Hajimete no basho de wa, tomadou mono da yo. Boku mo sō datta.
lines.meaning: It was your first day. A new place can feel confusing. Mine did too.

lines.speaker: Kenta
lines.line: レンはどうした？　{新人|しんじん}の{心得|こころえ}とか、ある？
lines.romaji: Ren wa dō shita? Shinjin no kokoroe toka, aru?
lines.meaning: What did you do? Any tips for someone new?

lines.speaker: Ren
lines.line: まず、{分|わ}からないことをメモしておくことだね。{後|あと}で{聞|き}けるように。
lines.romaji: Mazu, wakaranai koto o memo shite oku koto da ne. Ato de kikeru yō ni.
lines.meaning: First, note down what you don’t understand, so you can ask later.

lines.speaker: Kenta
lines.line: {今日|きょう}のことはメモしたよ。でも、{聞|き}くタイミングが{難|むずか}しい。
lines.romaji: Kyō no koto wa memo shita yo. Demo, kiku taimingu ga muzukashii.
lines.meaning: I did note it down today. It’s finding the right moment to ask that’s hard.

lines.speaker: Ren
lines.line: {明日|あした}、{開店|かいてん}{前|まえ}に{集|あつ}まるんだよね？　そのとき、{店長|てんちょう}に{聞|き}いてみたら。
lines.romaji: Ashita, kaiten mae ni atsumaru n da yo ne? Sono toki, tenchō ni kiite mitara.
lines.meaning: You meet before opening tomorrow, right? Why not ask the manager then?

lines.speaker: Kenta
lines.line: うん。あ、それなら{聞|き}けそう。{同|おな}じことでまた{止|と}まりたくないし。
lines.romaji: Un. A, sore nara kikesō. Onaji koto de mata tomaritakunai shi.
lines.meaning: Yes. Oh, I could ask then. I don’t want to get stuck on the same thing again.

lines.speaker: Ren
lines.line: {一人|ひとり}で{抱|かか}え{込|こ}まないことだ。レジの{後|うし}ろに{列|れつ}ができる{前|まえ}に、{声|こえ}をかけよう。
lines.romaji: Hitori de kakaekomanai koto da. Reji no ushiro ni retsu ga dekiru mae ni, koe o kakeyō.
lines.meaning: Don’t keep it all to yourself. Ask before a queue forms behind the till.

lines.speaker: Kenta
lines.line: {助言|じょげん}、ありがとう。レンもレジで{困|こま}ったことあるの？
lines.romaji: Jogen, arigatō. Ren mo reji de komatta koto aru no?
lines.meaning: Thanks for the advice. Have you ever had trouble at a till?

lines.speaker: Ren
lines.line: あるよ。{前日|ぜんじつ}に{習|なら}ったボタン、{次|つぎ}の{日|ひ}にはすっかり{忘|わす}れちゃって。
lines.romaji: Aru yo. Zenjitsu ni naratta botan, tsugi no hi ni wa sukkari wasurechatte.
lines.meaning: I have. I’d completely forgotten which button I’d learned the day before.

lines.speaker: Kenta
lines.line: それ、ちょっと{安心|あんしん}した。{明日|あした}はメモをポケットに{入|い}れていく。
lines.romaji: Sore, chotto anshin shita. Ashita wa memo o poketto ni irete iku.
lines.meaning: That makes me feel a bit better. Tomorrow I’ll keep my notes in my pocket.

lines.speaker: Ren
lines.line: いいね。{先輩|せんぱい}が{教|おし}えてくれたら、「ありがとう」も{忘|わす}れずにね。
lines.romaji: Ii ne. Senpai ga oshiete kuretara, arigatō mo wasurezu ni ne.
lines.meaning: Good. And remember to say thanks when someone shows you.

dialogues.title: A film invitation and a promised draft
dialogues.scene: On Thursday afternoon, Misaki invites Bao to a four-thirty film. Bao is finishing the newsletter revision promised to Yamamoto by five. They choose Friday’s six o’clock screening instead.

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: {今日|きょう}の{四時半|よじはん}、{映画|えいが}どう？　まだ{席|せき}、{空|あ}いてるよ。

lines.meaning: Fancy the film at four thirty today? There are still seats.

lines.speaker: You

lines.romaji: Ikitai kedo, sōkō no suikō ga mada owattenai n da.
lines.meaning: I’d like to, but I haven’t finished revising the draft.

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: {題名|だいめい}、{決|き}まったんじゃなかった？
lines.romaji: Daimei, kimatta n ja nakatta?
lines.meaning: Hadn’t you settled on a title?

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: {題名|だいめい}は{決|き}まったよ。{本文|ほんぶん}に{二人|ふたり}のコメントを{入|い}れたから、{最後|さいご}に{校正|こうせい}しなきゃ。
lines.romaji: Daimei wa kimatta yo. Honbun ni futari no komento o ireta kara, saigo ni kōsei shinakya.
lines.meaning: I have. I added the two comments to the text, so it needs a final proofread.

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: {掲載|けいさい}は{月曜日|げつようび}だよね。{今日|きょう}じゃなくてもいいんじゃない？
lines.romaji: Keisai wa getsuyōbi da yo ne. Kyō ja nakute mo ii n ja nai?
lines.meaning: It comes out on Monday, right? Doesn’t that mean it can wait?

lines.line: でも、{山本|やまもと}さんに{今日|きょう}の{五時|ごじ}までって{約束|やくそく}したから。{途中|とちゅう}で{出|で}かけるわけにはいかないよ。
lines.romaji: Demo, Yamamoto-san ni kyō no goji made tte yakusoku shita kara. Tochū de dekakeru wake ni wa ikanai yo.
lines.meaning: But I promised Yamamoto-san I’d send it by five today. I can’t head out halfway through.

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: そっか。{責任感|せきにんかん}、{強|つよ}いね。じゃあ、{今日|きょう}は{断念|だんねん}する？

lines.meaning: I see. You take your commitments seriously. Shall we give today a miss?

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: うん。{映画|えいが}が{嫌|きら}いなわけじゃないよ。これを{出|だ}したら、ゆっくり{見|み}たい。
lines.romaji: Un. Eiga ga kirai na wake ja nai yo. Kore o dashitara, yukkuri mitai.

lines.speaker: Misaki

lines.speaker: Misaki

lines.romaji: Yoyaku shitoku ne. Owattara renraku shite.
lines.meaning: I’ll book it. Message me when you’ve finished.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: うん。これなら、ゆっくり{見|み}られそう。{今度|こんど}こそ{予告|よこく}にも{間|ま}に{合|あ}いたいな。
lines.romaji: Un. Kore nara, yukkuri miraresō. Kondo koso yokoku ni mo maniaitai na.
lines.meaning: Yes. This way I can relax and enjoy it. This time I’d like to catch the trailers too.

watch.prompt: Optionally read or watch a scene from your own media in which someone gives advice or refuses an invitation. Identify the listener and reason; decide what is suggested, what is denied and what must still be done.

exercises.prompt: When does Kenta decide to ask about the till?
options: At tomorrow’s meeting before the shop opens
After tomorrow’s customers form a queue
Only after Ren has left the shop
exercises.explain: Ren suggests the pre-opening meeting, and Kenta says he could ask then.

exercises.prompt: What does Ren recall forgetting?
options: The title of Bao’s newspaper article
A button he had learned the day before
A promise to book cinema seats
exercises.explain: His memory is 前日に習ったボタン, and the following day he forgot it.

exercises.prompt: Which part of Ren’s advice had Kenta already followed that day?
options: Thanking Ren at the shop’s till
Making a note of what he didn’t understand
exercises.explain: Kenta says 今日のことはメモしたよ before they discuss when to ask.

exercises.context: Form practice: choose the taught expression of a common tendency, not a recommendation to feel confused.
exercises.line: {初|はじ}めての{場所|ばしょ}では、{戸惑|とまど}う＿＿。
exercises.explain: ものだ presents the tendency. Advisory ことだ would recommend the action, and わけがない denies its possibility.

exercises.context: Form practice: use the plain verb before advisory ことだ.
exercises.line: {早|はや}く{慣|な}れたいなら、{分|わ}からないことを＿＿ことだ。
exercises.explain: Advisory ことだ attaches to the dictionary form 聞く. This explicitly tests formation.

exercises.context: Reply casually to Ren. You accept his suggestion to ask the manager at the meeting tomorrow morning.
exercises.line: {明日|あした}、{開店|かいてん}{前|まえ}に{店長|てんちょう}に{聞|き}いてみたら。
options: うん。{明日|あした}は{誰|だれ}にも{聞|き}かないことにするよ。
ううん。{映画|えいが}の{予約|よやく}はレンに{任|まか}せるよ。
うん。メモを{見|み}せて、{聞|き}いてみるよ。
exercises.explain: Showing the notes and asking implements the proposal. The others reject it or switch to an unrelated subject.

exercises.meaning: If you’re unsure, my advice is not to keep everything to yourself.
exercises.explain: The negative verb before ことだ advises against taking everything on alone.

exercises.prompt: What made the queue longer on the first day?
options: The writer kept trying to work it out alone
The manager required every customer to take notes
The writer asked the manager before opening
exercises.explain: The first paragraph explicitly links thinking alone with the growing queue.

exercises.prompt: What did the writer put in the notebook after talking to their brother?
options: A complete list of every rule at the shop
A request to cancel the next shift
exercises.explain: They changed their plan for a long list and wrote three questions first.

exercises.prompt: What did the writer do differently the next afternoon?
options: Avoided the till by leaving before work started
Spent longer trying to solve it alone
Asked for help earlier when the same problem occurred
exercises.explain: The third paragraph says 今度は早めに声をかけた.

exercises.prompt: Which screening do they choose?
exercises.explain: They switch from today’s four-thirty film to tomorrow’s six o’clock showing; the scene is Thursday.

exercises.prompt: Why can’t Bao go out for the first screening?
options: Yamamoto said he must never go to films
He promised to finish and send the revision by five
Misaki has already bought seats for Monday
exercises.explain: He has a Thursday-five commitment; Monday is publication day.

exercises.prompt: What still needs checking after adding the comments?
options: Whether a title has been chosen at all
Whether the comments have ever been added
exercises.explain: The title is decided and comments are added. Final proofreading and checking numbers remain.

exercises.context: Form practice: complete the na-adjective attachment before わけじゃない.
exercises.line: {映画|えいが}が{嫌|きら}い＿＿わけじゃないよ。
exercises.explain: 嫌い is a na-adjective and uses 嫌いなわけじゃない in this attributive form.

exercises.context: Form practice: Bao must check the names because he promised. Choose the verb form that makes checking unavoidable.
exercises.line: {約束|やくそく}したから、{名前|なまえ}を＿＿わけにはいかない。
exercises.explain: 確認しないわけにはいかない means he has to check. 確認するわけにはいかない would block checking.

exercises.context: Reply casually to Misaki. Accept Friday’s six o’clock showing and explain that you’ll finish the draft first.
exercises.line: {明日|あした}の{六時|ろくじ}もあるよ。{私|わたし}はそっちでもいい。
options: ありがとう。{今日|きょう}の{四時半|よじはん}に{行|い}こう。
ううん。{映画|えいが}は{嫌|きら}いだから、もう{誘|さそ}わないで。
ありがとう。{草稿|そうこう}を{出|だ}してから、{明日|あした}{行|い}こう。
exercises.explain: The first accepts the proposed alternative and matches Bao’s plan. The other replies change the time or contradict his stated interest.

exercises.meaning: I promised, so I can’t go out leaving the draft unfinished.
tiles: {出|で}かけるわけにはいかない。
exercises.explain: The commitment blocks leaving. A positive dictionary verb before わけにはいかない has the opposite polarity to ないわけにはいかない.

exercises.prompt: Why isn’t Monday’s publication date enough to postpone the revision?
options: Other people need Friday for page layout
The newsletter is actually published Thursday afternoon
exercises.explain: The second paragraph explains Friday’s layout step and its required time.

exercises.prompt: What does changing the screening show about the writer’s intention?
options: They have given up on watching the film altogether
They still want to see the film after finishing the article
They no longer intend to finish the article
exercises.explain: The third and final paragraphs keep both the desire to watch and the intention to finish.

exercises.prompt: What would the writer prefer if an unexpected event made the deadline impossible?
options: Treat every promise as impossible to change
Wait until Monday without saying anything
Consult the other person early instead of silently being late
exercises.explain: The final paragraph recommends early consultation, while distinguishing this occasion when completion was feasible.
