lessons.title: Read the instructions for a new opening
lessons.description: Follow dates, required documents and formal occasion markers in a relocation notice.
lessons.canDo: Find the actions required on a significant occasion without confusing dates or attachment patterns

lessons.title: Who is included, and which case is singled out?
lessons.description: Separate inclusive eligibility, actual restrictions and an annoyed coincidence.
lessons.canDo: Keep participant scope, booking conditions and singled-out occasions distinct

grammar.title: Read an instruction tied to a significant occasion
grammar.formation: Event noun or dictionary-form verb + に際して/に際し. Before a noun: に際しての + noun. More polite spoken connector に際しまして.
grammar.explanation: に際して ties an action or instruction to a significant occasion, such as relocating a library. It is formal and fits a notice or prepared announcement. Do not add の after the event noun in this pattern. The earlier occasion can be recalled in a past-tense whole sentence, but the verb attached directly before に際して stays in its dictionary form.
grammar.example: 会員カードを発行するに際して、本人の名前を確認します。
grammar.translation: When issuing a membership card, we check the applicant’s name.

examples.ja: {会員|かいいん}カードを{発行|はっこう}するに{際|さい}して、{本人|ほんにん}の{名前|なまえ}を{確認|かくにん}します。
examples.en: When issuing a membership card, we check the applicant’s name.

examples.ja: {規約|きやく}の{改定|かいてい}に{際|さい}し、{変更|へんこう}{点|てん}を{掲示|けいじ}しました。
examples.en: On revising the terms, we posted the changes.

examples.ja: {移転|いてん}に{際|さい}しての{注意事項|ちゅういじこう}をお{読|よ}みください。
examples.en: Please read the instructions relating to the relocation.

grammar.mistake: Do not attach past 発行した directly before に際して or write 移転のに際して. The related noun phrase 移転の際に has a different attachment pattern. Do not treat にあたって as automatically wrong in an overlapping context.

grammar.title: Prepare for undertaking something important
grammar.formation: Event noun or dictionary-form verb + にあたって/にあたり. 当たって/当たり are possible written spellings.
grammar.explanation: にあたって often foregrounds preparations, intentions or measures when undertaking something important. It overlaps with に際して; a notice can often use either. The examples focus on opening or moving a facility, not an ordinary routine breakfast. The next clause supplies a purposeful action or instruction. The occasion marker itself does not indicate that the task has already been completed.
grammar.example: 新しい施設を開くにあたって、利用者の意見を聞いた。
grammar.translation: In preparing to open the new facility, we asked users for their views.

examples.ja: {新|あたら}しい{施設|しせつ}を{開|ひら}くにあたって、{利用|りよう}{者|しゃ}の{意見|いけん}を{聞|き}いた。
examples.en: In preparing to open the new facility, we asked users for their views.

examples.ja: {開会|かいかい}にあたり、{本日|ほんじつ}の{流|なが}れをご{説明|せつめい}します。
examples.en: At the opening, I’ll explain today’s programme.

examples.ja: {初|はじ}めて{参加|さんか}するにあたって、{募集|ぼしゅう}{要項|ようこう}を{確認|かくにん}してください。
examples.en: Before participating for the first time, please check the participation requirements.

grammar.mistake: Use a noun or dictionary verb, not 開くをにあたって. Nuance guides reading, but overlap means a quiz should not pit にあたって and に際して against each other as if only one could be grammatical.

grammar.title: Expand eligibility beyond the named group
grammar.formation: Noun + に限らず; the rest of the sentence expands the same scope, often using も.
grammar.explanation: に限らず means the named case or group is not the only one included. A workshop for 学生に限らず一般の方も includes non-students; it does not imply that every session has no capacity limit. Read separate conditions such as booking, date and number of seats as well. Familiar だけでなく often conveys a similar expansion in less formal wording.
grammar.example: 学生に限らず、一般の方も申し込めます。
grammar.translation: People who aren’t students can apply too.

examples.ja: {学生|がくせい}に{限|かぎ}らず、{一般|いっぱん}の{方|かた}も{申|もう}し{込|こ}めます。
examples.en: People who aren’t students can apply too.

examples.ja: {土曜日|どようび}に{限|かぎ}らず、{平日|へいじつ}も{利用|りよう}できます。
examples.en: It’s available on weekdays as well as Saturdays.

examples.ja: {館内|かんない}の{掲示|けいじ}に{限|かぎ}らず、ウェブサイトでも{告知|こくち}します。
examples.en: We’ll announce it online as well as on notices inside the building.

grammar.mistake: Do not infer that all other rules disappear. に限って restricts or singles out a case; に限らず expands it.

grammar.title: A restricted case or an awkward coincidence
grammar.formation: Noun + に限って. A time clause can modify a noun such as 日 or とき before this pattern. Formal に限り often marks a specified restriction.
grammar.explanation: Read the context to distinguish three uses: a service restricted to one stated case; an unwanted occurrence just on that occasion; and the speaker’s confidence that this particular trusted person would not do something. Today-only hours can be an actual condition. 今日に限って忘れた can be an annoyed coincidence, not proof of a repeated tendency. Person + に限って with a negative often expresses the speaker’s trust, not an established fact.
grammar.example: 説明会の当日に限って、九時に開館します。
grammar.translation: On the briefing day only, we’ll open at nine.

examples.ja: {説明会|せつめいかい}の{当日|とうじつ}に{限|かぎ}って、{九時|くじ}に{開館|かいかん}します。
examples.en: On the briefing day only, we’ll open at nine.

examples.ja: {今日|きょう}に{限|かぎ}って、{会員|かいいん}カードを{忘|わす}れちゃった。
examples.en: Of all days, I’ve forgotten my membership card today.

examples.ja: レンに{限|かぎ}って、{約束|やくそく}を{忘|わす}れるはずがない。
examples.en: Ren, of all people, wouldn’t forget a promise.

grammar.mistake: Do not read every に限って as a timetable restriction. に限らず means not limited to; the opposite direction. The formal wording に限り is taught here for notices, while に限る meaning “the best choice” is a separate construction.

dialogues.title: Make the relocation notice usable
dialogues.scene: The community library is moving next month. Yamamoto asks Bao to help with the notice for the next newsletter. They check the closing date, the new location and whether existing membership cards still work.

lines.speaker: Yamamoto
lines.line: {図書館|としょかん}の{移転|いてん}の{告知|こくち}、{次|つぎ}の{新聞|しんぶん}に{載|の}せたいの。{草稿|そうこう}を{見|み}てもらえる？
lines.romaji: Toshokan no iten no kokuchi, tsugi no shinbun ni nosetai no. Sōkō o mite moraeru?
lines.meaning: I’d like the library’s relocation notice in the next newsletter. Could you look at the draft?

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: はい。{題名|だいめい}は「{移転|いてん}に{際|さい}しての{注意事項|ちゅういじこう}」ですね。
lines.romaji: Hai. Daimei wa iten ni saishite no chūi jikō desu ne.
lines.meaning: Yes. The title’s “Instructions Relating to the Relocation,” isn’t it?

lines.speaker: Yamamoto
lines.line: ちょっと{硬|かた}いかしら。{中|なか}には{休|やす}む{日|ひ}と、{新|あたら}しい{場所|ばしょ}を{書|か}いてあるの。
lines.romaji: Chotto katai kashira. Naka ni wa yasumu hi to, atarashii basho o kaite aru no.
lines.meaning: Maybe that’s a bit stiff. It gives the closure dates and the new location.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: 「{図書館|としょかん}が{駅|えき}の{近|ちか}くに{移|うつ}ります」なら、すぐ{分|わ}かりそうです。
lines.romaji: Toshokan ga eki no chikaku ni utsurimasu nara, sugu wakarisō desu.
lines.meaning: “The Library Is Moving Near the Station” might be clearer at a glance.

lines.speaker: Yamamoto
lines.line: いいわね。{古|ふる}い{建物|たてもの}は{今月|こんげつ}の{二十日|はつか}までで、{新|あたら}しい{方|ほう}は{来月|らいげつ}の{一日|ついたち}からよ。
lines.romaji: Ii wa ne. Furui tatemono wa kongetsu no hatsuka made de, atarashii hō wa raigetsu no tsuitachi kara yo.
lines.meaning: That’s good. The old building’s open through the twentieth this month; the new one opens on the first next month.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: では、その{二|ふた}つの{日付|ひづけ}を{大|おお}きくしましょう。{場所|ばしょ}は{駅|えき}の{東口|ひがしぐち}ですね。
lines.romaji: Dewa, sono futatsu no hizuke o ōkiku shimashō. Basho wa eki no higashiguchi desu ne.
lines.meaning: Let’s make those two dates prominent. The new place is by the station’s east exit, right?

lines.speaker: Yamamoto
lines.line: ええ。{東口|ひがしぐち}から{歩|ある}いて{五分|ごふん}。{地図|ちず}もあると{助|たす}かるわ。
lines.romaji: Ee. Higashiguchi kara aruite gofun. Chizu mo aru to tasukaru wa.
lines.meaning: Yes, five minutes on foot from the east exit. A map would help too.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: {紙面|しめん}の{下|した}に{入|い}れられます。あ、{会員|かいいん}カードは{作|つく}り{直|なお}すんですか。
lines.romaji: Shimen no shita ni ireraremasu. A, kaiin kādo wa tsukurinaosu n desu ka.
lines.meaning: We can put one at the bottom of the page. Oh, do people need new membership cards?

lines.speaker: Yamamoto
lines.line: {今|いま}のカードをそのまま{使|つか}えるわ。{初|はじ}めて{登録|とうろく}する{人|ひと}は、{身分証|みぶんしょう}を{持|も}ってきてね。
lines.romaji: Ima no kādo o sono mama tsukaeru wa. Hajimete tōroku suru hito wa, mibunshō o motte kite ne.
lines.meaning: They can keep using their current cards. People registering for the first time should bring ID.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: {本人|ほんにん}の{名前|なまえ}を{確認|かくにん}するために、{提示|ていじ}してもらうんですね。
lines.romaji: Honnin no namae o kakunin suru tame ni, teiji shite morau n desu ne.
lines.meaning: They show it so their own name can be checked, then.

lines.speaker: Yamamoto
lines.line: そう。{新|あたら}しい{施設|しせつ}を{開|ひら}くにあたって、{案内|あんない}も{分|わ}かりやすくしたいの。
lines.romaji: Sō. Atarashii shisetsu o hiraku ni atatte, annai mo wakariyasuku shitai no.
lines.meaning: Exactly. As we open the new facility, I’d like the information to be easier to follow too.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: {掲載|けいさい}{前|まえ}に{校正|こうせい}します。{日付|ひづけ}と{地図|ちず}は、{特|とく}に{確認|かくにん}しておきますね。
lines.romaji: Keisai mae ni kōsei shimasu. Hizuke to chizu wa, toku ni kakunin shite okimasu ne.
lines.meaning: I’ll proofread it before publication, especially the dates and map.

dialogues.title: The opening day and the card left at home
dialogues.scene: On the new library’s opening day, Misaki and Bao read a workshop poster. The workshop is open beyond students but still requires booking. Bao has forgotten a membership card; he has ID and asks the desk about borrowing books.

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: ここ、{明|あか}るいね。{入口|いりぐち}のポスター、{文章|ぶんしょう}を{書|か}く{講座|こうざ}だって。
lines.romaji: Koko, akarui ne. Iriguchi no posutā, bunshō o kaku kōza da tte.
lines.meaning: It’s bright in here. That poster by the entrance is for a writing workshop.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: 「{学生|がくせい}に{限|かぎ}らず、{一般|いっぱん}の{方|かた}も」って{書|か}いてある。{山本|やまもと}さんも{来|こ}られそう。
lines.romaji: Gakusei ni kagirazu, ippan no kata mo tte kaite aru. Yamamoto-san mo korare sō.
lines.meaning: It says it’s for people who aren’t students too. Yamamoto-san could come.

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: {原則|げんそく}、{前日|ぜんじつ}までに{予約|よやく}だって。{思|おも}いつきで{来|く}るのはだめか。
lines.romaji: Gensoku, zenjitsu made ni yoyaku da tte. Omoitsuki de kuru no wa dame ka.
lines.meaning: As a rule, you book by the day before. So we can’t just turn up on a whim.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: うん。{二十人|にじゅうにん}までだしね。ノートを{持参|じさん}って、{家|いえ}ののでいいかな。
lines.romaji: Un. Nijūnin made da shi ne. Nōto o jisan tte, ie no no de ii kana.
lines.meaning: Yes, there are only twenty places. It says bring a notebook. Will my own one do?

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: いいんじゃない？　あ、{今日|きょう}に{限|かぎ}って、ペンのインクが{出|で}ない。
lines.romaji: Ii n ja nai? A, kyō ni kagitte, pen no inku ga denai.
lines.meaning: I’d think so. Oh, of all days, my pen’s not working today.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: {貸|か}すよ。これ、もう{一本|いっぽん}あるから。
lines.romaji: Kasu yo. Kore, mō ippon aru kara.
lines.meaning: Have mine. I’ve got another one.

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: ありがとう、{助|たす}かった。{先|さき}に{館内|かんない}を{見|み}ようか。
lines.romaji: Arigatō, tasukatta. Saki ni kannai o miyō ka.
lines.meaning: Thanks, that helps. Shall we look around first?

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: そうしよう。あれ、{会員|かいいん}カードがない。{今日|きょう}に{限|かぎ}って{忘|わす}れちゃった。
lines.romaji: Sō shiyō. Are, kaiin kādo ga nai. Kyō ni kagitte wasurechatta.
lines.meaning: Let’s. Huh, I haven’t got my membership card. Of all days, I’ve forgotten it today.

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: {本|ほん}を{借|か}りたいんだよね。{身分証|みぶんしょう}なら{持|も}ってる？
lines.romaji: Hon o karitai n da yo ne. Mibunshō nara motteru?
lines.meaning: You want to borrow a book, right? Have you got ID?

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: {持|も}ってる。でも、{貸出|かしだし}にはカードが{必要|ひつよう}って{案内|あんない}にあるよ。
lines.romaji: Motteru. Demo, kashidashi ni wa kādo ga hitsuyō tte annai ni aru yo.
lines.meaning: I have. But the information says you need your card to borrow books.

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: {例外|れいがい}があるか、{受付|うけつけ}で{聞|き}いてみよう。なければ、{今日|きょう}はここで{読|よ}めばいいし。
lines.romaji: Reigai ga aru ka, uketsuke de kiite miyō. Nakereba, kyō wa koko de yomeba ii shi.
lines.meaning: Let’s ask the desk if there’s an exception. If there isn’t, we can read here today.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: うん。{今日|きょう}だけ{開館|かいかん}が{早|はや}くて、{時間|じかん}もあるしね。
lines.romaji: Un. Kyō dake kaikan ga hayakute, jikan mo aru shi ne.
lines.meaning: Yes. It opened early just for today, so we’ve got time.

readings.title: The library’s relocation notice
paragraphs: {地域|ちいき}{図書館|としょかん}は、{来月|らいげつ}の{一日|ついたち}から{新|あたら}しい{建物|たてもの}での{利用|りよう}を{開始|かいし}します。{新|あたら}しい{施設|しせつ}を{開|ひら}くにあたって、{次|つぎ}の{通|とお}りご{案内|あんない}します。{現在|げんざい}の{建物|たてもの}は{今月|こんげつ}{二十日|はつか}の{午後|ごご}{六時|ろくじ}まで{利用|りよう}できます。{二十一日|にじゅういちにち}から{月末|げつまつ}までは{移転|いてん}{作業|さぎょう}のため{休館|きゅうかん}します。

{新|あたら}しい{図書館|としょかん}は{駅|えき}の{東口|ひがしぐち}から{徒歩|とほ}{五分|ごふん}です。{正面|しょうめん}の{入口|いりぐち}は{公園|こうえん}に{向|む}いています。{駅|えき}からの{地図|ちず}を、この{告知|こくち}の{下|した}とウェブサイトに{掲載|けいさい}しました。{広報|こうほう}{紙|し}をお{持|も}ちでない{方|かた}も、{入口|いりぐち}の{掲示|けいじ}で{確認|かくにん}できます。

{通常|つうじょう}の{開館|かいかん}{時間|じかん}は{午前|ごぜん}{九時半|くじはん}から{午後|ごご}{六時|ろくじ}までです。ただし、{開館|かいかん}{初日|しょにち}だけは{午前|ごぜん}{九時|くじ}から{利用|りよう}できます。{館内|かんない}の{設備|せつび}を{紹介|しょうかい}する{短|みじか}い{説明|せつめい}は、{初日|しょにち}の{九時|くじ}と{十時|じゅうじ}に{入口|いりぐち}から{始|はじ}めます。{説明|せつめい}を{聞|き}かずに{入館|にゅうかん}することもできます。

{移転|いてん}に{際|さい}して、{会員|かいいん}カードを{作|つく}り{直|なお}す{必要|ひつよう}はありません。{現在|げんざい}のカードをそのままお{使|つか}いください。{本|ほん}を{借|か}りる{場合|ばあい}はカードの{提示|ていじ}をお{願|ねが}いします。{初|はじ}めて{登録|とうろく}する{方|かた}は、{本人|ほんにん}の{名前|なまえ}が{確認|かくにん}できる{身分証|みぶんしょう}をお{持|も}ちください。カードの{発行|はっこう}は{無料|むりょう}です。

{休館|きゅうかん}{中|ちゅう}は{古|ふる}い{建物|たてもの}の{返却|へんきゃく}ボックスをご{利用|りよう}ください。{本|ほん}を{新|あたら}しく{借|か}りることはできません。{今回|こんかい}の{移転|いてん}についてご{質問|しつもん}がある{方|かた}は、{図書館|としょかん}の{受付|うけつけ}にご{連絡|れんらく}ください。{案内|あんない}の{準備|じゅんび}にご{協力|きょうりょく}くださった{皆様|みなさま}に、お{礼|れい}を{申|もう}し{上|あ}げます。

glosses.meaning: when undertaking; in preparation for this opening
can use; is available for use
closure of a library or similar facility
opening a library or similar building

glosses.text: 入館することもできます
glosses.kana: にゅうかんすることもできます
glosses.meaning: you can also enter the building

glosses.kana: ごきょうりょくくださった

readings.title: A workshop open beyond students
paragraphs: {新|あたら}しい{図書館|としょかん}で「{小|ちい}さな{記事|きじ}を{書|か}こう」という{講座|こうざ}を{開|ひら}きます。{開催|かいさい}{日|び}は{来月|らいげつ}の{最初|さいしょ}の{日曜日|にちようび}、{開会|かいかい}は{午前|ごぜん}{十時|じゅうじ}、{閉会|へいかい}は{十一時|じゅういちじ}です。{学生|がくせい}に{限|かぎ}らず、{一般|いっぱん}の{方|かた}も{参加|さんか}できます。{住|す}んでいる{地域|ちいき}による{限定|げんてい}はありません。{文章|ぶんしょう}を{書|か}いた{経験|けいけん}の{少|すく}ない{方|かた}も{歓迎|かんげい}します。

{定員|ていいん}は{二十人|にじゅうにん}です。{原則|げんそく}として、{前日|ぜんじつ}の{午後|ごご}{五時|ごじ}までにウェブサイトか{受付|うけつけ}で{予約|よやく}してください。{参加|さんか}{費|ひ}は{無料|むりょう}ですが、{予約|よやく}は{必要|ひつよう}です。{学生|がくせい}だけを{優遇|ゆうぐう}する{枠|わく}や、{当日|とうじつ}の{追加|ついか}{枠|わく}はありません。{予約|よやく}が{完了|かんりょう}した{方|かた}には、{受付|うけつけ}{番号|ばんごう}をお{知|し}らせします。

{当日|とうじつ}は、{受付|うけつけ}{番号|ばんごう}、ノート、ペンを{持参|じさん}してください。{会員|かいいん}カードは{参加|さんか}{資格|しかく}の{確認|かくにん}には{使|つか}いません。ただし、{本|ほん}の{貸出|かしだし}にはカードが{必要|ひつよう}です。{名前|なまえ}を{名簿|めいぼ}と{照|て}らし{合|あ}わせてから、{二階|にかい}の{講座|こうざ}{室|しつ}へご{案内|あんない}します。{名前|なまえ}の{表記|ひょうき}が{違|ちが}う{場合|ばあい}は、{早|はや}めにお{知|し}らせください。

{初|はじ}めに{短|みじか}い{草稿|そうこう}を{書|か}き、{二人|ふたり}で{読|よ}み{合|あ}います。{感想|かんそう}や{助言|じょげん}を{聞|き}いてから{推敲|すいこう}し、{最後|さいご}に{題名|だいめい}を{考|かんが}えます。{作品|さくひん}を{新聞|しんぶん}に{掲載|けいさい}するかどうかは{本人|ほんにん}が{後|あと}で{決|き}められます。{講座|こうざ}に{出|で}た{人|ひと}の{文章|ぶんしょう}を{自動|じどう}{的|てき}に{公開|こうかい}するわけではありません。

{講座|こうざ}の{当日|とうじつ}に{限|かぎ}り、{二階|にかい}の{部屋|へや}に{入|はい}れるのは{九時半|くじはん}からです。{図書館|としょかん}そのものの{開館|かいかん}{時間|じかん}とは{別|べつ}なので、ご{注意|ちゅうい}ください。{都合|つごう}が{悪|わる}くなった{方|かた}は、{前日|ぜんじつ}までに{取消|とりけし}のご{連絡|れんらく}をお{願|ねが}いします。

glosses.meaning: let’s write; invitation to write in the workshop title
will hold, of a workshop here
written form; spelling of a name here
only in this stated case, formal restriction

glosses.kana: つごうがわるくなった
glosses.meaning: can no longer make it; became unavailable

grammar: restriction and coincidence に限って
watch.prompt: Optionally read a notice from your own media or a real event you are considering. Mark who may participate, what must be done beforehand and any dates that apply only once. Compare the formal wording with how you would tell a friend.

recycling.reason: The relocation and workshop notices need new dates, eligibility and membership language. Recent draft/newsletter and advice words are retained only where they fit the actual scene or notice; the 27 percent target avoids inserting unrelated material into the spoken conversations.

exercises.prompt: Which two dates does Bao want to make prominent?
options: The old building’s final day and the new building’s first day
The workshop’s first and last applications
The newsletter’s last year and next year
exercises.explain: He proposes highlighting the twentieth of this month and the first of next month.

exercises.prompt: Where is the new library?
options: Beside the old building’s west door
Five minutes on foot from the station’s east exit
exercises.explain: Yamamoto states 東口から歩いて五分.

exercises.prompt: What happens to existing membership cards?
options: All holders must get new cards before next month
Only students can retain their cards
They can be used as they are
exercises.explain: Yamamoto says 今のカードをそのまま使える.

exercises.context: Form practice: choose the verb form that attaches directly before に際して.
exercises.line: {会員|かいいん}カードを＿＿に{際|さい}して、{名前|なまえ}を{確認|かくにん}します。
exercises.explain: Dictionary 発行する attaches before this occasion marker; the question explicitly tests attachment.

exercises.context: Form practice: complete the direct noun attachment for the taught opening marker にあたり.
exercises.line: ＿＿、{本日|ほんじつ}の{流|なが}れをご{説明|せつめい}します。
exercises.explain: 開会 attaches directly with にあたり. No を or が is inserted.

exercises.context: Reply politely to Yamamoto. You agree to check the dates and map before the notice is published.
exercises.line: {日付|ひづけ}と{地図|ちず}も、{掲載|けいさい}{前|まえ}に{見|み}てくれる？
options: はい。{掲載|けいさい}{後|ご}まで、どちらも{見|み}ません。
ううん。{映画|えいが}の{予約|よやく}なら{終|お}わったよ。
はい。{掲載|けいさい}{前|まえ}に、どちらも{確認|かくにん}します。
exercises.explain: Only the first accepts both checks and the requested timing in a polite response.

exercises.meaning: In preparing to open the new facility, we explained the outline of the plan.
tiles: {新|あたら}しい{施設|しせつ}を
{計画|けいかく}の{概要|がいよう}を
exercises.explain: The dictionary verb 開く connects to the occasion marker; 説明した supplies the whole sentence’s past tense.

exercises.prompt: When can someone no longer use the old building, before the new one opens?
options: From the twenty-first through the end of this month
From the first through the twentieth next month
Only from nine to ten on opening day
exercises.explain: The first paragraph identifies the relocation closure period.

exercises.prompt: What should someone registering for the first time bring?
options: A new card already issued by the old library
An identity document showing their own name
Only a map of the station’s west exit
exercises.explain: The fourth paragraph asks for 本人の名前が確認できる身分証.

exercises.prompt: How can borrowed books be returned during the closure?
options: Borrow another book at the new building first
Attend the new facility’s introduction session
Use the return box at the old building
exercises.explain: The final paragraph allows returns via the old box, while new borrowing is unavailable.

exercises.prompt: Why does Bao think Yamamoto could attend the workshop?
options: The poster explicitly includes people who aren’t students
Every resident automatically has a reserved place
Yamamoto is required to issue new membership cards
exercises.explain: 学生に限らず、一般の方も expands the participant group; it does not remove booking.

exercises.prompt: What has Bao forgotten?
options: The notebook required for a workshop already underway
exercises.explain: He has ID but cannot find his membership card.

exercises.prompt: What will they do about borrowing books?
options: Assume ID automatically replaces the card
Leave without asking and never return
Ask the desk whether there is an exception
exercises.explain: Misaki proposes asking; if there is no exception, they can read inside. No exception is established in the scene.

exercises.context: Form practice: choose the expression that includes non-students as well as students.
exercises.line: {学生|がくせい}＿＿、{一般|いっぱん}の{方|かた}も{参加|さんか}できます。
exercises.explain: に限らず expands the group; the other two restrict it.

exercises.context: Form practice: use the taught expression for an annoying coincidence on this particular day.
exercises.line: ＿＿、{会員|かいいん}カードを{忘|わす}れちゃった。
exercises.explain: The first singles out this awkward day. Not limited to today would change the scope; に限る has a different construction.

exercises.context: Reply casually to Misaki. You agree to ask the desk first, then read inside if borrowing without a card isn’t allowed.
exercises.line: {例外|れいがい}があるか、{受付|うけつけ}で{聞|き}いてみよう。
options: うん。もう{例外|れいがい}があるって{決|き}まったね。
ううん。{学生|がくせい}ならカードは{絶対|ぜったい}にいらないよ。
うん。だめだったら、{今日|きょう}は{館内|かんない}で{読|よ}もう。
exercises.explain: The first follows the plan without inventing an exception or a student rule.

exercises.meaning: We’ll announce it online as well as on notices inside the building.
tiles: {館内|かんない}の{掲示|けいじ}に{限|かぎ}らず、
exercises.explain: The first noun phrase plus に限らず expands the communication channels.

exercises.prompt: A non-student wants to attend. Which plan meets the stated conditions?
options: Book by five the preceding day and bring the booking number, notebook and pen
Come without booking because only students need reservations
Bring a membership card instead of making a reservation
exercises.explain: Eligibility extends beyond students; the same booking and required items still apply.

exercises.prompt: Does attending automatically publish the participant’s article?
options: Yes; every draft is published before the workshop closes
No; the participant can decide later whether to publish it
Only students’ articles must be published automatically
exercises.explain: The fourth paragraph assigns the later decision to 本人 and rejects automatic publication.

exercises.prompt: When can workshop participants enter the second-floor room that day?
options: From the preceding day at five
exercises.explain: The final paragraph distinguishes room access from the building’s opening hours.
